The e-ID is voluntary and is meant to help people prove who they are safely online, for example with the authorities.

begriffe.erklaerung: A graphic figure that represents a person online.
A program that stores many passwords securely encrypted.
Someone uses stolen data to pretend to be another person.
An electronic identity document you can use to prove who you are online.

gewusst: Passwords such as 123456 are among the most used every year and are cracked in seconds.
A password made of four random words is often more secure than a short password with lots of special characters.

teile.einleitung: The postman brings letters and parcels to people's homes. In Switzerland he is also called a Pöstler.
wichtigste: The **postman** brings letters and parcels.
In Switzerland people also say **Pöstler** or Pöstlerin.
He puts the post into people's **letter boxes**.
Postmen and postwomen work for **Swiss Post**.
Many ride a small electric vehicle or go on foot.
The **address** and the postcode show where a letter has to go.

abschnitte.text: Postmen and postwomen, in Switzerland also called **Pöstler**, deliver the post. They bring **letters**, newspapers and **parcels** to houses. They put small items into the **letter box**. They bring bigger parcels right to the front door. If nobody is in, they leave a collection notice.

Postmen are outdoors every day, in sunshine, rain and snow. Many ride a small **electric vehicle** from house to house. In some neighbourhoods they go on foot or ride a bike. In the morning they collect the post from the **delivery office**. There it has been sorted beforehand, so that it arrives in the right order.

For a letter to arrive in the right place, it needs an exact **address**. This includes the name, the street with the house number and the town with the **postcode**. In Switzerland the postcode has four digits. Over time the postman gets to know his round very well. He often knows exactly where each letter box is.

gewusst: Swiss postcodes were introduced in 1964.
In Switzerland there is A-Post and B-Post: A-Post usually arrives the next working day, while B-Post takes a little longer and is cheaper.

teile.einleitung: An app is a program for a mobile phone or a tablet. With apps you can play, chat, listen to music, learn or check the timetable. The word comes from the English “application”.
wichtigste: An app is a program for a mobile phone or tablet.
Apps are usually downloaded from the app store.
You open an app by tapping its icon.
The age rating shows from what age an app is suitable.
Even free apps can cost money through purchases in the app.
Before you download a new app, you ask your parents.
Updates make sure that apps stay safe.
Apps you no longer need are deleted.

abschnitte.text: An **app** is a computer program that runs on a smartphone or tablet. Each app has a particular job, for example taking photos, writing messages or showing the weather. On the screen you see each app as a small picture called an **icon**. If you tap on it, the app opens. Some apps are already installed when you buy the phone, for example the camera or the calendar.

Apps are usually downloaded from an **app store**. On iPhones it is called the App Store, on Android phones the Google Play Store. Apple opened its App Store in 2008, and Google followed shortly afterwards. Today there are millions of apps there. The stores check the apps, but even so not every app is good or safe.

Every app has an **age rating**. It shows from what age an app is suitable, for example because of violence or because of chats with strangers. Many social networks only allow you to sign up from the age of 13. Before you download a new app, you ask your parents. With parental controls, parents can set which apps are allowed.

Many apps are free but still earn money. This works, for example, through **in-app purchases**, that is, purchases inside the app, such as new game characters or coins. Other apps show advertising or collect data about their users. Some require a **subscription** that costs money every month. That is why it is important to protect purchases on your phone with a password.

Apps are regularly improved with **updates**. Updates close security gaps, so you should install them. An app often asks for **permissions**, for example for the camera or your location. You should only allow what the app really needs. It is best to delete apps you no longer use; this saves storage space and protects your data.

begriffe.erklaerung: Short for “application”, a program for a mobile phone or tablet.
An online shop where you can download apps.
A purchase made inside an app, for example for game coins.
A new version of an app that fixes mistakes and makes it safer.
Allowing an app, for example, to access the camera or your location.

gewusst: In the USA, the word “app” was chosen as word of the year 2010.
The MeteoSwiss app sends severe weather warnings straight to your phone.

teile.einleitung: Information security means protecting data and computer systems against theft, manipulation and failure. It is important for private individuals, schools, hospitals, companies and the state. That is because cybercriminals are constantly looking for weak points.
wichtigste: Information security protects the confidentiality, integrity and availability of data.
Spear phishing is a phishing attack tailored specifically to one person or company.
Ransomware encrypts data and demands a ransom.
A zero-day vulnerability is a weak point for which there is not yet a patch.
In a DDoS attack, many hijacked devices flood a server with requests.
Since 2024 the Federal Office for Cyber Security (NCSC) has been responsible in Switzerland.
Since 1 April 2025 operators of critical infrastructure have had to report cyber attacks within 24 hours.

abschnitte.text: Experts name three important goals of **information security**. **Confidentiality** means that only authorised people may see the data. Integrity means that data is not changed without anyone noticing, and availability means that systems work when you need them. A hospital, for example, must be able to access patient data at any time, but no outsider may read it.

In **phishing**, fraudsters try to get passwords and bank details with fake emails or websites. In spear phishing, the attack is tailored specifically to a particular person or company. The message then mentions, for example, the real names of work colleagues and so seems very believable. That is why you should always check links and attachments critically.

**Ransomware** is malware that encrypts data and then demands a ransom for decrypting it. In May 2017 the ransomware WannaCry infected hundreds of thousands of computers worldwide, including in hospitals in Great Britain. It exploited a gap in the Windows protocol SMB, for which there was already an update, but many people had not installed it. That is why regular updates and backup copies are very important.

A **zero-day vulnerability** is a weak point for which there is not yet a patch, that is, no repair from the manufacturer. The developers had, so to speak, zero days to fix it. In a **DDoS attack**, many hijacked devices send so many requests to a server at the same time that it is overloaded. The website can then no longer be reached by normal visitors.

**Two-factor authentication** asks for a second proof as well as the password, for example a code from an app on your phone. Long, different passwords and a password manager make attackers’ work harder. You should install updates for your phone, computer and apps quickly. It is best to save important files on another storage device as well.

Since 1 January 2024 the **Federal Office for Cyber Security** (BACS in German, NCSC in English) in Bern has been responsible for the cyber security of the Confederation. It grew out of the former National Cyber Security Centre. Anyone can report cyber incidents and attempted fraud to it. Since 1 April 2025 operators of critical infrastructure such as energy or water suppliers have had to report cyber attacks to the office within 24 hours.

begriffe.erklaerung: Fishing for passwords with fake messages.
Extortion software that encrypts data and demands a ransom.
An update that closes a security gap.
An attack in which a server is flooded with requests.

gewusst: The spread of WannaCry was slowed when a young security researcher happened to find a kind of emergency switch in the program code.
Most successful cyber attacks do not begin with clever technology, but with a person who clicks on the wrong link.

teile.einleitung: Cybergrooming means that adults deliberately seek contact with children and young people on the internet in order to manipulate them and harm them later, often with sexual intentions. The offenders pretend to be good friends or to be young themselves. If you know the tricks, you can protect yourself better.
wichtigste: In cybergrooming, adults deliberately build up trust with children online in order to harm them.
Offenders often pretend to be the same age and give compliments or presents.
Contact happens in chats, social networks and online games.
If someone you only know online wants to meet you, tell your parents or a trusted person and do not go alone.
Secrets that you are not allowed to tell anyone are a warning sign.
Those affected are never to blame themselves.
Help is available from Pro Juventute on the number 147 and from the police.

abschnitte.text: The English word **grooming** really means “caring for” or “preparing”. In **cybergrooming**, adults try to win the trust of children or young people over the internet. Their aim is to manipulate the children and exploit them sexually. This often happens gradually over weeks or months. Cybergrooming is not harmless fun but a serious danger.

Offenders often pretend to be **the same age** and use fake profile pictures. They give lots of compliments, listen and act as if they understand you especially well. Sometimes they give game currency, credit or extras for games. Later they ask for photos, private information or a meeting. They often ask you to keep everything secret and to move to a private chat.

Cybergrooming can happen anywhere you can write to strangers online. This includes social networks, messenger apps and **chats in online games**. Especially when gaming, a feeling of team spirit and friendship quickly develops. That is why it is important to stay careful with strangers. Setting your profile to “private” helps you to be contacted less by strangers.

You should be careful if someone asks for photos, your address or your school. If someone says that something should stay “our **secret**”, that is also a clear warning sign. A strange feeling in your stomach is an important signal and should be taken seriously. If someone you only know online wants to meet you, tell your parents or a **trusted person**. Never go to such a meeting alone.

Anyone affected is **never to blame themselves**, even if they have already sent pictures. Help is available from parents, teachers or from Pro Juventute on the telephone number 147, also by chat. You should save chat histories with screenshots and not delete them. The police take such cases very seriously, because they may be criminal offences. Afterwards you should block the contact and report it to the platform.

begriffe.erklaerung: When adults build up trust with children online in order to harm them.
An adult you trust, for example a parent or a teacher.
A picture of the screen that you can use to show what was in the chat.
A feature that stops a person from writing to you any more.

gewusst: Offenders often deliberately use online games, because children are relaxed there and like playing with others.
On the number 147 you can get help around the clock, free of charge and confidentially.

teile.einleitung: Chimney sweeps clean chimneys and heating systems. They make sure that fireplaces and boilers work safely and that no fires break out. Their black clothing is famous all over the world.
wichtigste: Chimney sweeps traditionally wear black clothing.
Soot from the chimney shows up less on black.
They clean chimneys, stoves and heating systems.
They check whether heating systems are safe.
The apprenticeship as a chimney sweep EFZ lasts three years.

abschnitte.text: Chimney sweeps traditionally wear **black clothing**. Cleaning chimneys produces a lot of **soot**. This black dust shows up less on black. The traditional formal outfit also includes a tall black hat, the **top hat**.

When wood, oil or gas burns, soot is produced. It builds up in the **chimney**. Too much soot can catch fire and cause a **chimney fire**. That is why chimney sweeps clean chimneys, stoves and boilers regularly. For this they use brushes, balls on ropes and vacuum cleaners.

Chimney sweeps also **check** whether heating systems are working properly. They measure the exhaust gases and test whether the system is giving off too many pollutants. In this way they protect the people in the house and the **environment**. In Switzerland the **cantons** decide how often heating systems must be cleaned and checked.

The apprenticeship as a **chimney sweep EFZ** lasts three years. You should have a head for heights, because some of the work takes place on the roof. Carefulness and enjoying contact with customers are also important. After the apprenticeship, further training up to master chimney sweep is possible.

gewusst: Chimney sweeps are seen as bringers of good luck. Many people are pleased when they meet one.
At New Year you often see the chimney sweep as a lucky symbol on cards and chocolate.

teile.einleitung: A hairdresser cuts, colours and styles hair. She advises her customers, and for this she needs skilful hands, a good eye and enjoyment of contact with people.
wichtigste: A hairdresser needs scissors and a comb every day.
She often uses a hairdryer as well.
She washes, cuts, colours and styles hair.
A good conversation with the customer is part of it.
In Switzerland the apprenticeship as a hairdresser EFZ lasts three years.

abschnitte.text: **Scissors** and a **comb** are a hairdresser's most important tools. With the comb she divides the hair into sections, and with the scissors she cuts. For short hair she often uses **hair clippers**. With the **hairdryer** and a round brush she dries and shapes the hairstyle. For curls or straight hair there are curling tongs and straighteners.

Before she cuts, the hairdresser asks what the customer would like. She looks at the hair and gives tips on which hairstyle would suit. She also explains how to look after the hair at home. A friendly conversation makes the customer feel comfortable.

Many customers have their hair **coloured** or **tinted**. The hairdresser mixes the colour according to a recipe and applies it with a brush. While doing so she wears **gloves** to protect her skin. She also knows a lot about shampoo, conditioner and other **care products**.

In Switzerland you learn the job in the apprenticeship as a **hairdresser EFZ**. It lasts three years. You work in the salon and attend **vocational school**. There you also learn about skin, hair and chemistry. After the apprenticeship you can train further, for example with a professional examination.

gewusst: Good hairdressers look after their scissors carefully and have them sharpened regularly.
Hair grows about one centimetre a month.

teile.einleitung: Retail specialists work in shops, for example in a supermarket, a sports shop or a bookshop. They advise customers, work at the till and make sure the goods are neatly arranged on the shelves.
wichtigste: A retail specialist advises customers and sells in the shop.
She fills up the shelves and puts goods away.
She also works at the till.
The apprenticeship as a retail specialist EFZ lasts three years.
There is also a two-year apprenticeship with a Federal VET Certificate.
The retail apprenticeship is one of the most frequently chosen apprenticeships in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: **Retail** means selling goods directly to customers. Retail specialists receive new deliveries and check them. Then they put the goods away and fill up the **shelves**. They make sure everything is displayed attractively and clearly. They remove products that are out of date or damaged from sale.

An important task is giving **advice**. Someone looking for new walking boots, for example, gets tips on size and material. For this, retail specialists know their products well. They are friendly, listen and find suitable solutions. They stay polite even when customers complain.

At the **till** they scan the goods and take cash or cards. In the evening the till is cashed up so that everything adds up. Today many shops also sell online. That is why orders from the **online shop** are more and more often part of the work.

The apprenticeship as a **retail specialist EFZ** lasts three years. You work in the shop and attend **vocational school**. Depending on the company, you get to know a particular **sector**, such as food, sport or electronics. For young people who prefer to learn in a practical way, there is the two-year apprenticeship as a **retail assistant EBA**. After the apprenticeship you can train further, for example to become a branch manager.

gewusst: The German word Detailhandel (retail) comes from the French “en détail”, meaning in small quantities.
The retail apprenticeship exists in a great many different sectors.

teile.einleitung: Media are all the means by which people spread information, stories and entertainment, from newspapers, radio and television to smartphones, apps and social networks. Today children and young people in Switzerland spend a lot of time online every day. If you know the opportunities and dangers, you can use media wisely, safely and with enjoyment.
wichtigste: Media spread information, opinions and entertainment.
Almost all young people in Switzerland have their own smartphone.
According to their rules, TikTok, Instagram and Snapchat only allow an account from the age of 13.
An algorithm chooses which videos you see, depending on what you watch.
You may only put photos of other people on the internet with their consent.
Many apps are free because they make money from advertising and your data.
If something on the internet frightens you, tell an adult you trust.

abschnitte.text: In the past people got their information mainly from **newspapers**; later radio arrived in the 1920s and television in the 1950s. Since the 1990s the internet has spread, and since the first iPhone in 2007 almost everyone has carried the internet around in their pocket. Today the media are merging: newspapers appear online, and people watch television programmes on their phones. The JAMES study by the ZHAW (Zurich University of Applied Sciences) regularly shows that almost all young people in Switzerland have a smartphone.

On TikTok, Instagram or YouTube an **algorithm** decides which videos you see next. It remembers what you watch for a long time, like or share, and shows you more of it. This creates an endless stream of content that can easily keep you there much longer than planned. Sometimes this means you only see one side of a topic; this is called a **filter bubble**.

Not everything on the internet is true. If a news story surprises you, check the source and see whether reliable media such as the “Tagesschau” news report the same thing. With artificial intelligence it is now possible to make **deepfakes**, fake pictures, videos or voices that seem real. With pictures, a reverse image search can sometimes help you find out where they come from.

Only put photos of other people on the internet if the person agrees, because everyone has the **right to their own image**. If someone is repeatedly picked on in a group chat, that is **cyberbullying**. Then it helps to take screenshots, block or report the person and involve someone you trust. Children and young people can get help around the clock from Pro Juventute on the number 147.

Many apps are free because they make money from advertising and from their users' data. The more an app knows about you, the more precisely it can show you adverts. If an influencer is paid by a company for a post, the post should be clearly recognisable as advertising. Taking a critical look helps you notice when someone wants to sell you something.

Media offer many opportunities: learning, being creative, keeping up friendships and discovering the world. At the same time, too much screen time, especially in the evening, can disturb sleep and concentration. Experts recommend screen-free times, for example during meals and before going to bed. If you take breaks on purpose and agree on rules with your family, you use media in the healthiest way.

begriffe.erklaerung: The ability to use media safely, critically and sensibly.
A set of calculation rules that decides which content you see.
A picture, video or voice faked with AI that seems real.
You only see content that matches your own opinion.
Repeatedly picking on someone on the internet.

gewusst: The JAMES study on how Swiss young people use media has been published every two years since 2010.
Switzerland's first radio programme went on air in the 1920s.
Many mobile phones show in their settings exactly how many hours a day you spend looking at the screen.

teile.einleitung: Personal data is any information that reveals something about you, for example your name, your address or your date of birth. On the internet such data is valuable, and some people want to misuse it. If you protect your data well, you are much safer online.
wichtigste: Personal data is information about a particular person, such as name, address or phone number.
You never tell a stranger on the internet your address.
In games it is best to use a made-up name instead of your real name.
Photos are personal data too, because they can show who you are and where you are.
Before you send a photo of a friend, you ask her for permission.
Once something has been on the internet, it is not certain to be completely gone after deleting.
In Switzerland the Data Protection Act protects personal data.

abschnitte.text: **Personal data** is any information that belongs to a particular person. It includes your name, your address, your phone number, your date of birth and your school. Photos, voice messages or the location of your phone also count. Information about health, religion or passwords is especially sensitive, because it reveals a lot about a person.

You do not share your address, phone number, date of birth or the name of your school with strangers on the internet. Online anyone can pretend to be a child, even if they are really an adult. That is why you choose a **made-up name** such as “Starfox12” for games and chats. You can happily show harmless things such as your favourite colour or your favourite animal.

A photo in front of your school or your house reveals where you often spend time. Some mobile phone photos even invisibly store the place where they were taken. Before you send a photo of a friend, you always ask that person first. That is because everyone has the **right to their own image**.

A deleted photo is not certain to be completely gone. Other people may have taken a **screenshot** first or forwarded the picture. Some sites also store copies on their servers. That is why the rule is: only post what your grandparents or your teacher could see too.

In Switzerland the **Data Protection Act** (DSG) regulates how companies and authorities must handle personal data. Since September 2023 a new, stricter version of this law has applied. Everyone may, for example, ask what data a company has stored about them. Compliance is monitored by the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC) in Bern.

begriffe.erklaerung: Rules that protect personal data from misuse.
An invented name that reveals nothing about you.
A picture of the screen taken with a phone or computer.
The place where you are right now, which your phone can detect.

gewusst: With just three pieces of information, date of birth, sex and postcode, many people can be identified clearly.
Many free apps earn their money by collecting data about their users.
Your voice in a voice message also counts as personal information.

teile.einleitung: A digital business model describes how a company earns money on the internet. Many apps and platforms are free, but they too have to make an income. If you know the models, you understand better why apps work the way they do.
wichtigste: A business model describes how a company earns money.
In the freemium model, basic functions are free and extra functions cost money.
On ad-funded free platforms, you pay with your attention and your data.
In real-time bidding, advertising spaces are auctioned in milliseconds.
Subscriptions bring regular income; the churn rate shows how many customers cancel.
In affiliate marketing, you earn a commission through recommendation links.
The theory of the long tail says that niche products are also worthwhile online.

abschnitte.text: Many platforms such as search engines and social networks are free for users. They earn their money with **advertising**, which is why you pay there with your attention and your data. The more a platform knows about its users, the more precisely it can target advertising. An important price is the **cost per thousand** (CPM): at 5 francs per 1000 views, 2 million views cost 10,000 francs.

In **real-time bidding**, an advertising space is auctioned while a website is loading. Various advertisers bid on it automatically, depending on who is visiting the page at that moment. The whole thing takes only a fraction of a second. The winner may show its advert to exactly this person.

In the **freemium** model, basic functions are free, and you pay for extra functions or for no advertising. Many games earn their money with in-app purchases, for example for game characters or virtual coins. Streaming services for music and films rely on monthly **subscriptions**. The churn rate is important for them: if a service with 10,000 subscribers loses 500 in a month, it is 5 per cent.

Marketplaces and booking websites often earn a fee for every sale or booking. In **affiliate marketing**, someone receives a commission when something is bought through their recommendation link. Many influencers and comparison websites use this model. For buyers this is not always obvious at first glance.

In 2004 the journalist Chris Anderson made the theory of the **long tail** well known. It says that online it is also worthwhile to sell many niche products in small quantities, because there is no shop shelf limiting space. Another principle is the **network effect**: a platform becomes more valuable the more people use it. That is why some platforms become very large and hard to push aside.

begriffe.erklaerung: A mixture of free and premium: the basic version is free, extras cost money.
The price for 1000 views of an advert.
The share of customers who cancel within a certain time.
Advertising through recommendation links in return for a commission.

gewusst: A well-known saying goes: if you are not paying for a product, you are the product.
In German, long tail is called “langer Schwanz”; it describes the shape of a sales curve.

teile.einleitung: Anyone doing an apprenticeship does not only work at the company. On one or two days a week, apprentices go to vocational school.
wichtigste: As well as working at the company, apprentices go to **vocational school**.
The official name is **Berufsfachschule** (vocational school).
At vocational school you learn the knowledge for your own job.
There are also **general subjects** such as language, politics and sport.
You usually go to school one to two days a week.
The rest of the time you work at the **training company**.

abschnitte.text: In Switzerland many young people do an **apprenticeship** after compulsory schooling. In it they learn in two places. At the **training company** they work alongside others and learn the practical side. At **vocational school** they learn the theory. The official name is **Berufsfachschule**.

At vocational school apprentices learn the **knowledge** they need for their job. A cook, for example, learns which nutrients are in food. An electrician learns how electricity works. In addition there are **general subjects** such as language, politics and economics. **Sport** is part of it too.

You usually go to vocational school **one to two days** a week. The rest of the time you work at the company. The school day counts as **working time**, so your pay is not reduced. If you want to and have good marks, you can also do the **vocational baccalaureate**. Then you attend more school days.

gewusst: Apprentices in the same class often come from many different companies and places.
Compulsory lessons at vocational school cost the apprentices nothing.

teile.einleitung: An apprenticeship trade is a job that you learn in Switzerland through basic vocational training. There are about 250 apprenticeship trades, from commercial employee to electrician to mediamatics specialist.
wichtigste: In Switzerland there are about 250 apprenticeship trades.
An apprenticeship with EFZ lasts three or four years, one with EBA two years.
The commercial apprenticeship is by far the most common; in 2020 more than 12,000 young people began a KV apprenticeship.
Healthcare assistant (FaGe) and retail specialist are also among the most popular apprenticeships.
FaBe stands for childcare and social care worker (Fachfrau or Fachmann Betreuung).
After an EBA apprenticeship you can often go on to a shortened EFZ apprenticeship.

abschnitte.text: Apprenticeship trades end with one of two qualifications. You gain the **EFZ**, the Federal VET Diploma, after three or four years. You gain the **EBA**, the Federal VET Certificate, after two years. The EBA apprenticeship is somewhat more practical and suits young people who find school harder. Afterwards you can often add a **shortened** EFZ apprenticeship.

The **commercial apprenticeship**, KV for short, has been the most common apprenticeship in Switzerland for years. According to the Federal Statistical Office, more than 12,000 young people began an apprenticeship as a **commercial employee EFZ** in 2020. Next come **healthcare assistant** (FaGe), with almost 5000 new apprentices in 2020, and **retail specialists**, who advise customers and manage goods.

Many apprenticeship trades are about people. **FaGe** care for and look after patients in hospitals and care homes. **FaBe**, social care workers, work for example in Kitas, old people's homes or with people with disabilities. The two-year basic training as a **health and social care assistant EBA** (AGS) supports people in their everyday lives.

**Electricians** lay cables and fit switches, sockets and systems. Their apprenticeship lasts four years. The apprenticeship as a **mediamatics specialist EFZ** also lasts four years. It combines computing, multimedia and marketing: mediamatics specialists design websites and videos and look after computers.

If you like being outdoors, you will also find many apprenticeship trades, for example farmer, gardener or forestry worker. In farming there is the two-year basic training as an **agricultural assistant EBA**. They help out on farms and in vegetable or fruit businesses. On the website **berufsberatung.ch** you can look at all the apprenticeship trades in Switzerland.

gewusst: About two thirds of young people in Switzerland do an apprenticeship after compulsory school.
With the vocational Matura you can study at a university of applied sciences after your apprenticeship.

teile.einleitung: Electricians make sure that the lights work in a house and that electricity comes out of the socket. In Switzerland the official name of the job is electrical installer (Elektroinstallateur).
wichtigste: An electrician lays cables and fits sockets.
The official name is electrical installer.
Without electricians there would be no light in the house.
Electricity is dangerous, so you work very carefully.
In Switzerland a socket has a voltage of 230 volts.

abschnitte.text: When a new house is built, electricians lay the **cables** in the walls and ceilings. They fit **sockets, switches and lights**. All the circuits come together in the **fuse box**. That is where the fuses are, which switch off the electricity if there is an overload. This protects the house from fires.

A Swiss socket supplies **230 volts**. That is enough to injure a person seriously. That is why electricians always switch off the electricity before they work and check that the circuit is really dead. A **residual current device**, called an FI in Switzerland, switches off the electricity in a flash if something is wrong. Children should never fiddle with sockets or cables themselves.

Today the work also includes **network cables**, alarm systems and charging stations for electric cars. Many houses have **solar panels** on the roof that need to be connected. In modern houses you can even control lights and blinds with your mobile phone. So electricians always have to keep learning new things.

The apprenticeship as an **electrical installer EFZ** lasts four years. There is also the three-year apprenticeship as an **installation electrician EFZ**. You learn at the company, at vocational school and in courses. Anyone who later wants to take responsibility for installations on their own needs further training with a federal diploma.

gewusst: Swiss plugs have their own shape, which does not fit in many other countries.
A residual current device reacts in a fraction of a second.

teile.einleitung: Caretakers, in Switzerland often called Abwart, look after buildings such as schools or blocks of flats. They make sure that everything is clean, safe and in order.
wichtigste: The caretaker looks after a building and its surroundings.
In Switzerland people often say Abwart.
He cleans, repairs small things and checks the technical systems.
In a school he is an important contact person.
The matching apprenticeship is called building maintenance specialist EFZ.

abschnitte.text: In the school, the **caretaker** makes sure that everything is clean and in one piece. He unlocks in the morning and locks up in the evening. He replaces broken lamps, repairs doors and sets out tables and chairs. When there are problems he is an important **contact person** for teachers and children.

A building has a lot of **technology**: heating, ventilation, water and electricity. The caretaker checks these systems regularly. He repairs small faults himself. For bigger problems he calls in specialists such as electricians or plumbers and keeps an eye on their work.

The **surroundings** are part of the job too. The caretaker mows the lawn, trims hedges and sweeps up the leaves. In winter he clears **snow** and spreads grit so that nobody slips. He makes sure that the rubbish is sorted and disposed of properly.

The apprenticeship as a **building maintenance specialist EFZ** lasts three years. You learn to clean, repair, look after things and use machines. Later you can do further training as a **caretaker with a federal certificate**. Practical skills and friendliness are important.

gewusst: In large housing estates there is often a whole team of caretakers.
The word Abwart is used mainly in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: A cook prepares the food for the guests in the restaurant kitchen. She chops, fries and cooks, and at the end the waiting staff bring the finished plates to the tables.
wichtigste: The cook prepares the food in the restaurant.
She works with knives, pans, pots, the oven and many other appliances.
Part of the work happens before the rush: the preparation, also called mise en place.
When the orders come in, everything has to happen quickly and accurately.
The kitchen and the waiting staff work closely together.
Women and men work in the kitchen equally.

abschnitte.text: The working day begins with the **mise en place**, the preparation. The cook chops onions, prepares vegetables, makes stock and gets everything ready. When the restaurant opens, the **orders** come in. Now there is frying, cooking and arranging. After service the kitchen is cleaned thoroughly, and the cook plans the next day with the team.

A restaurant has two areas: the **kitchen** and the **service**. The waiting staff take the guests' orders and pass them on to the kitchen. When a dish is ready, the cook puts the plate on the **pass**. From there the waiting staff bring the food to the guest. For this to work, both teams have to talk to each other well.

A cook also thinks about many other things. She checks whether the delivered goods are fresh. She pays attention to **allergies**, because some guests cannot eat nuts or gluten, for example. She helps to plan the **menu** and works out how much she needs to buy. This way as little food as possible is thrown away.

Restaurants are open when other people are free. That is why cooks often work in the **evening**, at **weekends** and on public holidays. In return, many have time off during the week. There are also jobs with regular hours, for example in canteens. In Switzerland the apprenticeship is called **cook EFZ** and lasts three years.

gewusst: “Mise en place” is French and means roughly “putting everything in its place”.
The Frenchman Auguste Escoffier is seen as one of the most famous cooks in history and wrote a large cookbook with thousands of recipes.

teile.einleitung: A social bot is an automated account on a social network that posts, likes and comments like a person. But there is no person behind it, only a computer program. Social bots can be harmless, but they are also used to influence opinions.
wichtigste: A social bot is an automated account that posts like a person.
The word “bot” is short for “robot”.
Bots can spread thousands of posts in a short time.
With many bots, an opinion can be made to look bigger than it is.
Signs of bots include, for example, very many posts around the clock and no real profile picture.
With artificial intelligence, bots are becoming harder and harder to spot.
Not every bot is bad; some report the weather or earthquakes, for example.

abschnitte.text: A **social bot** is a computer program that runs its own account on social networks. It writes posts, hands out likes, follows other accounts and replies to comments, all automatically. Many such accounts pretend to be real people, with a name, a profile picture and a life story. The word **bot** is short for “robot”.

A bot follows rules set by programmers, for example: “Share every post with the hashtag XY”. Modern bots use **artificial intelligence** and can create whole sentences and even pictures themselves. Often a single person controls hundreds or thousands of bots at the same time. Such a network of many bots is called a **botnet**.

Because bots post without a break, they can make a topic artificially big. If thousands of accounts share the same opinion, it looks as if many people think that way. This is discussed especially before elections and votes, for example the US presidential election in 2016. Bots can also spread false news quickly or attack people with comments.

Signs of a bot are very many posts around the clock, even in the middle of the night. Often the account has no real profile picture, a strange name with lots of numbers and was only created recently. Bots often just share other people's content and react unusually quickly. But you can never be completely sure, so it is always worth checking claims against reliable sources.

Not all bots are harmful. Some accounts automatically publish weather warnings, earthquake reports or timetable changes. **Chatbots** on websites answer customers' questions. What matters is that a bot is honestly labelled as a bot, and many platforms now require this.

begriffe.erklaerung: A computer program that carries out tasks automatically.
Many bots that are controlled together.
A program you can have a conversation with in writing.
Computer programs that can learn and solve tasks the way people do.
A report that is not true but is meant to look genuine.

gewusst: Some bot accounts publish several hundred posts in a single day.
As early as 1950 the British mathematician Alan Turing thought about how to test whether a computer behaves like a human.
Big platforms delete millions of fake accounts every year.

teile.einleitung: A trade union is an association of employees. Together they work for good wages, fair working hours and safe jobs.
wichtigste: Measured by number of members, Unia is the largest trade union in Switzerland.
The Swiss Trade Union Federation was founded in 1880 and is the largest umbrella organisation.
A second umbrella organisation is called Travail.Suisse.
Article 28 of the Federal Constitution protects freedom of association.
The General Strike of 1918 was the largest strike in Swiss history.
The International Labour Organization ILO has its headquarters in Geneva.

abschnitte.text: A single person carries little weight compared with a large company. Many people together can achieve more. That is why employees join together in **trade unions**. These negotiate **collective labour agreements** with the employers, advise their members and help with disputes at work.

**Unia** was created in 2004 from the merger of several trade unions, including GBI and SMUV. It mainly represents workers in industry, construction, trades and services. The **VPOD**, the union of public service staff, represents employees in administration, schools and hospitals. Many trade unions belong to the **Swiss Trade Union Federation** (SGB), others to **Travail.Suisse**.

**Art. 28 BV** guarantees **freedom of association**, which is the right to join together in associations. Strikes and lockouts are allowed if they concern working relationships. However, they must not go against a duty to keep industrial peace, as many collective labour agreements contain.

From 12 to 14 November 1918, about 250,000 people stopped work in the **General Strike**. It was led by the **Olten Action Committee**. Among other things, it demanded the **48-hour week**, the AVS and votes for women. The 48-hour week was largely introduced in 1919/1920, the AVS only in 1948 and votes for women in 1971.

The **International Labour Organization** (ILO) was founded in 1919 and has its headquarters in **Geneva**. Today it is part of the United Nations. Its structure is special: governments, employers and workers all have a say together. The ILO works for fair working conditions around the world.

gewusst: The abbreviation SGB stands for the Swiss Trade Union Federation, the oldest umbrella organisation of employees in Switzerland.
The 1918 demand for votes for women was only met at federal level more than 50 years later.

teile.einleitung: Screen time is the time you spend in front of a mobile phone, tablet, computer or television. Screens are useful and fun, but too much of them is not good for your eyes, head and body. That is why good rules and enough breaks are important.
wichtigste: Screen time is the time spent in front of a mobile phone, tablet, computer or television.
Breaks from the screen are good for your eyes, head and body.
After a long time at a screen, exercise outdoors is ideal.
Phones and tablets are not a good idea just before going to sleep.
For children, parents help to decide on screen time.
An alarm or timer helps you to stop in time.
At the family dinner table, you put your phone away.

abschnitte.text: **Screen time** includes everything you do at a screen: watching videos, gaming, chatting or watching television. Homework on the computer really counts too. Many phones count screen time automatically and show it in the settings. The Swiss **JAMES study** regularly looks at how young people use media. It shows that almost all young people in Switzerland have their own mobile phone.

If you look at a screen for a very long time, your **eyes** are often tired and dry, because you blink less while doing so. Experts recommend the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look at something about 6 metres away for 20 seconds. Sitting for a long time can lead to tension in the neck and back. In children who spend a lot of time indoors and look closely at screens, the risk of **short-sightedness** also rises. Daylight outdoors protects the eyes.

Phones and tablets are not a good idea just before going to sleep. Exciting videos or games keep your head awake. The bright light of screens can also make it harder to fall asleep. That is why it is good to charge your phone outside the **bedroom** at night. A book or a story before sleep helps you to switch off.

For children, the **parents** decide how much screen time is allowed. A well-known guide is the **3-6-9-12 rule** of the French psychiatrist Serge Tisseron. It recommends no screen before the age of 3 and no games console of your own before 6. You should only go on the internet alone from 9 and on social networks only from 12. Another good family rule is to put your phone away at mealtimes.

A **timer** or alarm helps you to stop in time. Many phones have a feature that suggests a break after a certain time. After gaming, exercise outdoors is good, for example cycling or playing football. Board games, crafts, reading or making music are also great things to do without a screen. During breaks, body and mind recover.

begriffe.erklaerung: Time spent in front of a mobile phone, tablet, computer or television.
An eye problem in which things in the distance look blurred.
A rule of thumb about which screen media suit which age.
A Swiss study about how young people use media.

gewusst: When you look at a screen, you blink much less often than usual, which is why your eyes become dry.
Since 2010 the JAMES study has been carried out every two years by ZHAW together with Swisscom.

teile.einleitung: Hobbies are things you like doing in your free time. They can help you choose a career, because if you enjoy doing something, you may also find a job that suits it.
wichtigste: A hobby can show what kind of work you enjoy.
If you like building with wood, you may find a career as a cabinetmaker or carpenter.
Careers advice helps you choose a career.
In a taster apprenticeship you can try out a job.
Not every hobby has to become a job.

abschnitte.text: Tim likes building things with **wood** in his free time. This shows that he enjoys working with his hands and making something you can see. Jobs such as **cabinetmaker** or **carpenter** could suit him. A cabinetmaker builds furniture, doors and kitchens. A carpenter builds roof frames and wooden houses.

If you like drawing, you may find a job in design. If you like tinkering with bikes, you might be interested in a technical job. If you like looking after animals, you can become an animal keeper. The important thing is to ask yourself: **What do I enjoy?** and **What am I good at?**

In Switzerland every canton has a **careers advice service**. There you get information about many jobs and can have conversations with advisers. Many regions have a **careers information centre** (BIZ). Parents and teachers also help in the search for the right job.

In a **taster apprenticeship** you work for a few days in a company. This way you see what the job is really like day to day. Sometimes you notice that a hobby is even more fun as a job. Sometimes you also notice that you would rather keep it as a hobby. Both are valuable experiences.

gewusst: The apprenticeships as cabinetmaker EFZ and as carpenter EFZ each last four years.
In Switzerland there are about 250 different jobs that you can learn through an apprenticeship.

teile.einleitung: Automotive mechatronics technicians service and repair cars, vans or lorries in a garage. They combine mechanics, electrics and electronics, because modern vehicles are full of computers and sensors. In Switzerland it is a popular apprenticeship leading to the Federal VET Diploma (EFZ).
wichtigste: Automotive mechatronics technicians repair cars in a garage.
In Switzerland the apprenticeship lasts four years and ends with the EFZ.
There are two specialisms: passenger cars and commercial vehicles.
With diagnostic devices they find faults in vehicles' electronics.
Electric and hybrid cars are making the job more and more an electronics job.
Good results in maths and physics and a feel for technology are important.
After the apprenticeship there are many further training options, such as becoming an automotive diagnostician.

abschnitte.titel: What do you do in this job?
abschnitte.text: **Automotive mechatronics technicians** carry out servicing, change oil, brakes and tyres and repair faulty parts. Above all, though, they look for faults in complicated systems such as engine management, air conditioning or driver assistance. To do this they connect **diagnostic devices** to the vehicle's on-board computer. Afterwards they test whether everything is working perfectly again.

The apprenticeship as an automotive mechatronics technician **EFZ** lasts four years. You work in a garage, attend vocational school and learn further basics in inter-company courses. There are the specialisms **passenger cars** and **commercial vehicles**, for example lorries and buses. The training is the responsibility of the industry association AGVS, the Swiss Automotive Trade Association.

For this job you need a feel for technology, enthusiasm for vehicles and skilful hands. Good knowledge of **maths**, physics and electrical engineering is important, because you have to understand measurements and read circuit diagrams. Logical thinking helps too, because looking for faults is often like detective work. If you are unsure, you can get to know the job through a **taster apprenticeship**.

Modern cars contain dozens of small computers called control units. With **electric cars** and hybrid vehicles, knowledge of high-voltage batteries and electric motors is becoming more and more important. Working on high-voltage systems requires special training, because high voltages are dangerous. Driver assistance systems such as cameras and radar sensors must also be precisely adjusted after a repair.

After the apprenticeship you can, for example, train further as an **automotive diagnostician** with a federal certificate. A vocational baccalaureate and a degree at a university of applied sciences, for example in vehicle engineering, are also possible. If you would prefer shorter training, you can become an automotive specialist EFZ in three years. For young people who learn in a more practical way, there is also the two-year apprenticeship as an automotive assistant EBA.

begriffe.erklaerung: Federal VET Diploma, the qualification at the end of a three- or four-year apprenticeship.
A combination of mechanics, electronics and computer science.
A computer that reads out faults in the vehicle.
A vehicle for transporting goods or many people, such as a lorry.
A few days at a company to get to know a job.

gewusst: A modern car can contain more lines of program code than a passenger plane.
The job used to be called car mechanic; the new name shows the important role of electronics.
In 2024 about 4.8 million passenger cars were registered in Switzerland, and they all need regular servicing.

teile.einleitung: At the checkout you pay for your shopping in the shop. There the goods are recorded, the prices are added up, and you pay with cash, card or mobile phone.
wichtigste: You pay at the checkout.
The goods are recorded with a scanner using the barcode.
You can pay with cash, card or mobile phone.
After paying you get a receipt.
Retail specialists also learn how to work at the checkout during their apprenticeship.

abschnitte.text: Every product has a **barcode** stuck on it. The **scanner** at the checkout reads it with light. The computer then knows immediately what the product costs. At the end the till adds all the prices together. You can see the total on the screen.

You can pay with **cash**, which means coins and notes in **francs** and centimes. If you give too much, you get **change** back. Today many people pay with a **card** or with their mobile phone. At the end you receive a **receipt**. It shows what you bought and how much you paid.

Today many shops also have **self-service checkouts**. There you scan the goods yourself and pay at the machine. Some shops have hand scanners that let you record everything while you are still shopping. Even so, staff help when something goes wrong.

If you work in a shop, you can do the apprenticeship as a **retail specialist EFZ**. It lasts three years. There is also the two-year apprenticeship as a **retail assistant EBA**. You learn to advise customers, stock shelves and work at the checkout. Friendliness and handling money accurately are important.

gewusst: Today the smallest coin in Switzerland is the 5-centime piece.
In the evening, the till is checked to see whether the money in the drawer matches the sales.

teile.einleitung: A search engine is a program on the internet that helps you find exactly what you are looking for among billions of web pages. You type in a few search words and get a list of results in a fraction of a second. The best-known search engine is Google, but there are also special search engines for children.
wichtigste: With a search engine you find web pages on a topic.
You type in search words, for example “animals forest Switzerland”.
The search engine shows a list of results.
The first results are not always the best; often there are adverts among them too.
If you cannot find anything suitable, other search words help.
With image search you find pictures for a search word.
There are special search engines for children, such as fragFINN or Blinde Kuh.

abschnitte.text: A **search engine** is like a huge table of contents for the internet. You enter search words, and it shows you a **list of results** with suitable web pages. As well as the normal search there is also image search, video search and map search. Well-known search engines are Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo and the Swiss service Swisscows.

Small programs called **crawlers** constantly travel through the internet and read web pages. The contents are stored in a huge directory, the **index**. When you search for something, the search engine looks through this index and ranks the results by importance. What counts here is, for example, how well a page matches the search word and how many other pages link to it.

Good search words are short and precise, for example “animals forest Switzerland” instead of a whole sentence. If you cannot find anything suitable, try other or additional search words. With quotation marks you search for an exact sequence of words, for example “Rütli Oath 1291”. Do not just read the first result, because the top results are sometimes paid adverts marked as “Ad”.

There are special **search engines for children** such as fragFINN, Blinde Kuh or Helles Köpfchen. They only show pages that have been checked beforehand and are suitable for children. Blinde Kuh has existed since 1997 and is seen as one of the oldest search engines for children. For younger children these services are a safe way to start searching the internet.

Google was founded in California in 1998 by the students **Larry Page** and Sergey Brin. Their idea was to rank pages by how often other pages refer to them. Today most searches worldwide go through Google. In Zurich, Google runs one of its largest development centres outside the USA.

begriffe.erklaerung: A word you type in to find something.
The list of results that a search engine displays.
A program that automatically reads and collects web pages.
A huge directory of all the web pages collected.

gewusst: The name Google comes from “googol”, a number written as a 1 followed by 100 zeros.
When people search for something on the internet, they often just say they “google” it; the German word “googeln” is even in the Duden dictionary.
Today AI chatbots also answer search questions directly with a text instead of a list of results.

teile.einleitung: The General Data Protection Regulation, GDPR for short, is a law of the European Union that governs the protection of personal data. It has applied since 25 May 2018 and is considered one of the strictest data protection laws in the world. Swiss companies must also follow it if they have customers in the EU.
wichtigste: The GDPR has applied throughout the EU since 25 May 2018.
It protects the personal data of people in the EU.
Because of the market location principle, it also applies to companies outside the EU, for example in Switzerland.
Fines can be up to 20 million euros or 4 per cent of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher.
Data breaches must usually be reported within 72 hours.
Users have rights such as access, erasure and data portability.
The highest fine so far, 1.2 billion euros, was imposed on the Meta group in 2023.

abschnitte.text: The **General Data Protection Regulation** was adopted in 2016 by the European Parliament and the Council of the EU. After a transition period of two years, it has applied since 25 May 2018. As a **regulation**, it applies directly in all member states, without each country having to make its own law. It replaced the older Data Protection Directive of 1995. In German it is called Datenschutz-Grundverordnung, DSGVO for short.

abschnitte.titel: Does it also apply to Switzerland?
abschnitte.text: Switzerland is not an EU member, but the GDPR still affects many Swiss companies. Under the **market location principle**, it applies to everyone who offers goods or services to people in the EU or observes their behaviour. So a Swiss online shop that delivers to Germany must follow it. At the same time, in 2023 Switzerland brought its own Data Protection Act closely into line with the GDPR. That is why the basic ideas are similar.

The GDPR gives every person important rights. With the **right of access** you can find out what data a company stores about you. The **right to erasure** allows you, under certain conditions, to have data deleted. Article 20 governs the right to **data portability**: you can receive your data in a common format and take it with you to another provider. You can also have incorrect data corrected.

Even before the GDPR, the European Court of Justice made an important ruling in 2014 in the **Google Spain** case. A Spanish man wanted old newspaper reports about his debts no longer to appear on Google. The court decided that search engines must remove links under certain circumstances. This gave rise to the so-called **right to be forgotten**. In the GDPR it is laid down in Article 17.

Companies may only process data if they have a legal reason, for example **consent**. If data is stolen or lost, the company must usually report this to the **supervisory authority** within 72 hours. Breaches can lead to fines of up to 20 million euros or 4 per cent of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher. In 2023 the Irish data protection authority imposed a record fine of 1.2 billion euros on Meta. The reason was the transfer of Facebook data to the USA.

The GDPR has visibly changed the internet. Since then many websites have asked for consent to **cookies**, although these banners are also based on other EU rules. Companies must explain in a privacy policy what data they collect. For many online services, children under 16 need their parents’ consent. However, individual countries may lower this limit to as low as 13.

begriffe.erklaerung: General Data Protection Regulation, the data protection law of the European Union.
The rule that the GDPR also applies to companies that offer something to people in the EU.
The right to get your data and take it with you to another provider.
The right to have certain data or search results deleted.
An office that checks whether data protection rules are being followed.

gewusst: The GDPR consists of 99 articles.
Many large tech companies have their European headquarters in Ireland, which is why the Irish data protection authority plays an especially important role.

teile.einleitung: If you like cooking at home and trying out new recipes, you can turn this into a job. The best-known job for this is cook.
wichtigste: If you like cooking, you can become a cook.
The apprenticeship as a cook EFZ lasts three years.
There is also a two-year training course as a kitchen assistant EBA.
Cooks work in restaurants, hotels, hospitals or canteens.
Other jobs also have to do with food, for example baker and confectioner.

abschnitte.text: At home, Sara likes nothing better than helping with the **cooking**. She enjoys trying out new recipes and likes it when everyone enjoys the food. The job of **cook** could suit her. In the three-year apprenticeship as a **cook EFZ** you learn to prepare dishes, present them nicely and work cleanly.

In a large kitchen a **team** works together. Each person has their own task: preparing vegetables, making sauces, frying meat or making desserts. Everything has to happen quickly when many guests eat at the same time. **Hygiene** is very important so that nobody gets ill.

Cooks often work when other people are eating: at lunchtime, in the evening and at the weekend. In return they sometimes have days off during the week. Places of work are **restaurants**, **hotels**, hospitals, care homes or canteens in companies and schools.

abschnitte.titel: Other jobs to do with food
abschnitte.text: If you prefer baking, you may find a job as a **baker and confectioner EFZ**. If you would like a shorter training course, you can become a **kitchen assistant EBA**. After the cooking apprenticeship you can train further, for example as a **diet cook**, who cooks food for people with special needs.

gewusst: At skills championships, young cooks from all over the world compete against each other.
In a professional kitchen people often call out “Service!” when a plate is ready.

teile.einleitung: The plane is a tool used to make wood smooth and straight. It takes thin shavings off the surface and is part of the basic equipment of cabinetmakers.
wichtigste: With a plane you make wood smooth and straight.
A sharp blade in the plane cuts off thin shavings.
You always plane in the direction of the wood grain.
Cabinetmakers often use the plane.
Today there are also electric planes and large planing machines.

abschnitte.text: A hand plane has a body made of wood or metal. A sharp **plane iron** sticks out a little at the bottom. When you push the plane over the board, the iron cuts off a thin **shaving**. The shaving often curls into a lovely ringlet. The less the iron sticks out, the finer the shaving.

You plane in the direction of the **wood grain**. If you plane against it, the wood tears and becomes rough. For this the board is clamped firmly onto a **workbench**. With even pressure you push the plane along the whole length. This makes the surface smooth and straight.

For large amounts of wood, joinery workshops use **planing machines**. With them, boards are quickly brought to the thickness you want. There are also **electric planes** that you guide by hand. But for fine work and repairs the hand plane remains important.

The apprenticeship as a **cabinetmaker EFZ** lasts four years. Cabinetmakers build furniture, kitchens, doors and windows. Besides the plane they need saws, drills, sandpaper and glue. Precision and a love of wood as a material are important.

gewusst: Tools similar to the plane have existed since Roman times.
The plane iron has to be sharpened regularly, otherwise the surface does not become nice and smooth.

teile.einleitung: The careers information centre, BIZ for short, is a place to go with all questions about jobs and training. Young people find information and personal advice there.
wichtigste: **BIZ** stands for **Berufsinformationszentrum**, the careers information centre.
The careers information centres are run by the **cantons**.
For young people choosing a job, the BIZ information library is usually **free of charge**.
At the BIZ there are job brochures, films and advice sessions.
Careers, study and career guidance advisers work there.
**Adults** can use the services too.

abschnitte.text: At the **careers information centre**, **BIZ** for short, you find information about jobs, training and further training. In Switzerland careers, study and career guidance is the responsibility of the **cantons**. That is why the BIZ centres belong to the cantonal services. Larger cantons often have several BIZ centres in different regions.

In the BIZ **information library** you can browse on your own. There are **job brochures**, folders and **films** about a great many jobs. You find out what you do in a job and what schooling you need. For young people choosing a job this is usually **free of charge**. In this way everyone has access to information about jobs.

Trained **careers, study and career guidance advisers** work at the BIZ. They hold **advice sessions** and help you recognise your own strengths and interests. They also show which paths lead to a job. The advisers support you, but you make the decision yourself.

If you are going to an advice session, you should prepare. It is best to write down your own **questions** and **interests** beforehand. **School reports** or reports from taster placements are also helpful. That way you make good use of the advice time. By the way, the BIZ is also there for **adults**, for example with questions about further training or changing jobs.

gewusst: Many school classes visit the BIZ together as part of their career choice lessons.
A lot of the information from the BIZ can also be found online at berufsberatung.ch.

teile.einleitung: Your digital footprint is all the traces you leave on the internet. Every post, every photo, every search and every click can be stored. These traces often stay visible for much longer than you think.
wichtigste: The digital footprint includes all the traces you leave on the internet.
There are traces you leave yourself, and traces that other people or apps collect about you.
The internet does not forget: once something is published, it can hardly be deleted completely.
Mobile phone photos can store the place where they were taken in their metadata.
Incognito mode only stops the history from being saved on your own device.
With the right to be forgotten, you can ask search engines to remove links.

abschnitte.text: Just like footprints in the snow, you also leave traces on the internet. Your **active footprint** includes everything you publish yourself, that is, posts, comments, photos and videos. Your **passive footprint** includes data that is collected without you doing much, for example websites visited, your location and searches. Websites often use small files called cookies for this.

A mobile phone photo contains not only the picture but also **metadata**. This can include the date, time, camera model and even the exact place where it was taken. If you share such a photo, you may give away where you live or go to school. Many platforms remove this data, but not all, and you can switch off location in the camera app.

A browser’s **incognito mode** does not save the history on your own device. But websites, your school, your employer or your internet provider can still see what you look at. So incognito only protects you from other people who use the same device. Apps that constantly record where you are also collect traces, so you should switch off location access where it is not needed.

Future training companies or employers sometimes search the internet for applicants. Public posts can be found through search engines, even after many years. An embarrassing photo or a nasty comment can therefore cause harm later. On the other hand, a good footprint with hobbies or projects can make a positive impression.

In app settings you can decide who sees your posts. It helps to think before posting whether you will still like the content in five years’ time. In Europe there is the **right to be forgotten**, with which you can ask search engines to remove certain links about you. Now and then it is worth typing your own name into a search engine and seeing what appears.

begriffe.erklaerung: Extra information in a file, for example the date or place a photo was taken.
A small file that websites use to recognise visitors.
A browser mode that does not save the history on the device.
The right to ask search engines to remove links.

gewusst: The right to be forgotten goes back to a ruling by the European Court of Justice in 2014.
Even people who post nothing themselves have a digital footprint, because others can share photos or names of them.

teile.einleitung: The federal diploma (eidgenössisches Diplom) is a demanding qualification in higher vocational education. You receive it after the advanced federal examination, which in the crafts is often called the master craftsman's examination.
wichtigste: The advanced federal examination leads to the federal diploma.
In the crafts it is often called the master craftsman's examination.
Many advanced federal examinations require a federal certificate and additional practical experience.
The federal government pays up to 10,500 francs towards the preparation courses.
In English the diploma is called the Advanced Federal Diploma of Higher Education.
Federal diplomas can often be recognised by the abbreviation “eidg. dipl.”.

abschnitte.text: The **advanced federal examination (HFP)** is the most demanding federal examination in higher vocational education. Anyone who passes it receives a **federal diploma**. It sets higher requirements than the professional examination. The HFP is aimed at professionals who want to **run a business** or work as an **expert**.

In craft trades the advanced federal examination is known as the **master craftsman's examination**. Anyone who passes it holds a title such as “eidg. dipl. Schreinermeister” (master carpenter with federal diploma). Other diplomas do not carry a master title, for example the **certified tax expert** or the **electrical installation and safety expert**. What they all have in common is the abbreviation **“eidg. dipl.”**.

The HFP often builds on the **professional examination**. That is why many examination regulations require a **federal certificate** and additional work experience. Some diplomas are even a requirement for certain kinds of work. Under the **Low-Voltage Installation Ordinance (NIV)**, in the electrical field you count as qualified if you have passed the advanced federal examination as an electrical installation and safety expert. Only then do you receive a general **installation permit**.

The federal government refunds **half** of the eligible course fees for preparation. Fees of up to 21,000 francs are counted, so the contribution is at most **10,500 francs**. Internationally the diploma is called the **Advanced Federal Diploma of Higher Education**. The word “Advanced” shows the higher level compared with the federal certificate.

gewusst: With an EFZ alone you may not take responsibility for installations on your own in the electrical field.
The federal contribution for the advanced federal examination is higher than for the professional examination.

teile.einleitung: Universities of applied sciences (Fachhochschulen) are universities with a strong practical focus. They train professionals, for example in engineering, business, health, social work or art, and in Switzerland they are one of the three types of university.
wichtigste: The Universities of Applied Sciences Act was passed in 1995.
Switzerland has eight public universities of applied sciences (as of 2025).
The standard entry route is a vocational baccalaureate in a related job.
A bachelor's degree comprises 180 ECTS credits, that is three years of full-time study.
Bachelor's programmes have existed since autumn 2005.
Universities of applied sciences cannot award a doctorate on their own.

abschnitte.text: On **6 October 1995** parliament passed the **Federal Act on Universities of Applied Sciences**. As a result, around 70 former higher technical colleges were merged into universities of applied sciences. With the **Bologna reform**, the universities of applied sciences switched to bachelor's programmes from **autumn 2005**. Most master's programmes followed from 2008. Before that there were titles such as “Ingenieur FH” (engineer, university of applied sciences).

abschnitte.titel: Eight public universities of applied sciences
abschnitte.text: In 2025 there are eight public universities of applied sciences: **BFH, HES-SO, FHNW, HSLU, SUPSI, OST, ZFH** and, since 2020, the **University of Applied Sciences of the Grisons**. **HES-SO** is a network of institutions in the cantons of western Switzerland and one of the largest universities of applied sciences. **SUPSI** is the university of applied sciences of Italian-speaking Switzerland, with sites in Ticino. There are also private universities of applied sciences.

The classic route to a university of applied sciences is an **apprenticeship with a vocational baccalaureate** in a suitable occupational field. That is why it is called the royal road. Other qualifications are also possible, for example an academic Matura with a year of work experience or a specialised baccalaureate. However, additional conditions apply.

A **bachelor's degree** comprises **180 ECTS credits**, which corresponds to three years of full-time study. 60 ECTS credits are awarded per year of study. After that you can do a **master's degree**. Only universities may award a **doctorate**. Universities of applied sciences only offer doctoral programmes in cooperation with universities.

Universities of applied sciences also offer further training for people in work. A **CAS** (Certificate of Advanced Studies) is the smallest form, with at least **10 ECTS credits**. A **DAS** has at least 30 and a **MAS** at least 60 ECTS credits. Many people study part-time alongside their job.

gewusst: Since 2020 the University of Applied Sciences of the Grisons has been the youngest public university of applied sciences.
One ECTS credit corresponds to about 25 to 30 hours of work.

teile.einleitung: When you are looking for an apprenticeship, many companies ask for an aptitude test. It shows whether you meet the school and other requirements of a job, and it helps companies choose.
wichtigste: An aptitude test checks whether you meet the requirements of a job.
The Multicheck is widely used in German-speaking Switzerland.
Maths, language and logical thinking are often tested.
Spatial awareness and concentration can also come up.
You can prepare well with practice exercises.
Aptitude tests often cost money.

abschnitte.titel: What is an aptitude test for?
abschnitte.text: An **aptitude test** checks school knowledge and abilities such as logic or concentration. Many training companies use the results to compare applications. You usually include the report in your **application file**. A well-known test in German-speaking Switzerland is the **Multicheck**. There are different versions of it for different types of job.

Typical parts are **maths, German, foreign languages and logic**. In tasks on **spatial awareness** you have to turn shapes and solids around in your head. This is important in technical jobs, for example for draughtspeople or mechanics. In **concentration tasks** you might, for example, look for certain symbols quickly and without mistakes. This shows whether you can work accurately over a longer time.

With **practice exercises** you get to know the kind of questions. This gives you confidence and saves time in the test. Before the test it helps to sleep well and eat enough. In the test you read the tasks carefully and do not let a difficult question hold you up for too long.

abschnitte.titel: If it does not go well
abschnitte.text: Many aptitude tests cost a **fee**, which is usually paid by the young people or their parents. In some cantons or companies there is support. A weak result is no reason to give up. A test only shows part of your abilities. You can often **retake** it and convince companies with good **taster placement reports**.

gewusst: There are different versions of the Multicheck depending on the type of job.
Good taster placement reports can be just as important to a company as a test result.

teile.einleitung: Anyone doing an apprenticeship in Switzerland learns in two places: at the training company and at vocational school. At school they learn the theory of their job and get general education.
wichtigste: Apprentices usually attend vocational school **one to two days** a week.
Under the Vocational and Professional Education and Training Act, compulsory lessons are **free of charge**.
Lessons count as working time, and the company must give time off **without deducting pay**.
Subjects include vocational knowledge, **general education** (ABU) and **sport**.
There are **support courses** for apprentices who find things difficult.
Those who do well can also attend **optional courses**.

abschnitte.text: The apprenticeship in Switzerland is called **dual vocational training**. Dual means that you learn in two places. At the **training company** you work alongside others and learn the practical side. At **vocational school** you learn the theory. As a rule you go to school one to two days a week. In many jobs there are also **inter-company courses**, in which you practise basic skills.

In **vocational lessons** you learn the theory of your own job, for example materials or job-specific maths. **General education**, ABU for short, covers topics such as law, politics, economics and language. Apprentices who are not doing the vocational baccalaureate attend ABU. **Sport** is also compulsory in vocational education and training.

According to the **Vocational and Professional Education and Training Act** (Art. 22 BBG), compulsory lessons at vocational schools are **free of charge**. The training company must give apprentices time off for compulsory lessons, **without deducting pay**. This is set out in Art. 345a OR. So a school day counts like a working day.

Anyone who struggles at school can attend **support courses**. There the material is explained and practised again. For those who are particularly interested there are **optional courses**, for example in languages. The company must allow them without deducting pay, as long as performance at work and at school is good. In this way everyone can learn according to their own abilities.

gewusst: Roughly two thirds of young people in Switzerland do vocational education and training after compulsory schooling.
At the end of the apprenticeship comes the qualification procedure, which used to be called the final apprenticeship examination.

teile.einleitung: Farmers make sure that we have milk, meat, grain and vegetables. Their work on the farm depends a great deal on the weather and the seasons.
wichtigste: Farmers look after animals and grow plants.
Today the job is officially called agricultural specialist (Landwirtin or Landwirt).
Many farms have cows, pigs or hens.
Crops include, for example, grain, potatoes and vegetables.
The apprenticeship as a farmer EFZ lasts three years.
A lot of our food comes from farms.
