The **Federal Constitution** says that men and women have equal rights. They are entitled to **equal pay for work of equal value**. The **Gender Equality Act** also forbids anyone from being disadvantaged at work because of their sex. Whether these rules are put into practice well everywhere in everyday life is debated again and again in politics.

When **choosing a job**, it is worth looking at different jobs without prejudice. Doing a **taster placement** is the best way to find out whether a job suits you. On **Future Day**, which exists in many cantons, children can get to know jobs that are less typical for their sex. The careers advice service also helps you discover all the possibilities.

gewusst: The canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden only introduced the right to vote for women in 1990, after a ruling by the Federal Supreme Court.
In Switzerland many job titles exist in a female and a male form, for example Schreinerin and Schreiner (carpenter).

teile.einleitung: The tall white chef's hat is the best-known sign of the cooking profession. It looks good, but above all it has a practical job: it protects the food from hairs.
wichtigste: Cooks often wear a tall white chef's hat.
The hat keeps the hair together so that no hairs fall into the food.
In French the chef's hat is called a “toque”.
White shows straight away whether the clothing is clean.
Today many cooks also wear smaller hats, caps or hairnets.

abschnitte.text: In a kitchen, **hygiene** is very important. A hair in the food is unpleasant for guests and can carry germs. The **chef's hat** covers the head and keeps the hair together. It also soaks up some sweat, because it gets hot at the cooker. Because it is **white**, you can see stains straight away and know when it needs to go in the wash.

The tall, pleated hat is called a **toque** in French. It became well known in French cooking and today is a symbol of cooks all over the world. A well-known **legend** says that the many pleats stand for the many ways in which a good cook can prepare eggs. Whether this is true is not certain, but people like telling the story.

In everyday work many cooks no longer wear a tall toque, but a low **hat**, a **cap**, a headscarf or a **hairnet**. All that matters is that the hair is covered. Chef's clothing also includes the **chef's jacket** made of thick fabric, which protects against splashes, an apron and non-slip shoes.

gewusst: The chef's jacket often has two rows of buttons, so if it gets a stain you can button it the other way and it looks clean again.
The chef's hat is so well known that it is often used as a symbol for restaurants or cookbooks.

teile.einleitung: A recommender system is a computer program that suggests videos, songs, products or posts you might like. Such systems are found in streaming services, online shops and social networks. They have a big say in what we see on the internet.
wichtigste: Recommender systems suggest content that you might like.
Collaborative filtering recommends what similar users have liked.
Content-based filtering compares features of content with what you liked.
In the cold start problem, there is not yet any data for new users or new content.
Many algorithms optimise for interaction and time spent.
In 2011 Eli Pariser coined the term filter bubble.
The EU’s Digital Services Act requires an option without profiling.

abschnitte.text: A **recommender system** evaluates what you have watched, listened to, bought or liked. From this an **algorithm** calculates what will probably interest you too. Examples are the home page of video platforms, music suggestions or the note in an online shop telling you what other customers also bought. Without such systems, you could hardly find your way through the huge amount of content.

In **collaborative filtering**, the system looks for people with similar taste and recommends what they liked. In **content-based filtering**, it compares features such as genre, subject or artist with what you have already liked. Many services combine both methods and today also use artificial intelligence. One problem is the cold start: for new users or new content, there is not yet enough data for good recommendations.

In 2006 the streaming service Netflix launched a competition, the **Netflix Prize**. Whoever could improve the prediction accuracy of its own recommender system by 10 per cent was to receive 1 million US dollars. In 2009 an international team won the prize. The competition greatly advanced research into recommender systems.

Many recommendation algorithms of social networks are designed to create as much **interaction** and time spent as possible. The longer you stay, the more advertising can be shown. This can lead to especially exciting or extreme content being favoured. As a result, some people lose more time than they really wanted to.

If a system only ever suggests similar things, a **filter bubble** can form, a term coined by Eli Pariser in 2011. An **echo chamber** is something different: there, like-minded people strengthen each other themselves. The EU’s Digital Services Act requires very large platforms to offer at least one recommendation option that is not based on profiling. You can also steer against it yourself by deliberately looking for other content.

begriffe.erklaerung: A precise set of calculating instructions that a computer carries out step by step.
Recommendations based on what people with similar taste liked.
There is not yet enough data about newcomers for good recommendations.
Creating a personality profile from collected data.

gewusst: In 2009 the Netflix Prize was awarded to the team BellKor’s Pragmatic Chaos.
Even if you only watch a video briefly and swipe on, the algorithm learns something from it.

teile.einleitung: Internet fraud means tricks that criminals use on the internet to get other people’s money or data. The fraudsters use fake shops, false love stories or supposed prizes. If you know the scams, you can protect yourself well.
wichtigste: A fake shop is a fake online shop that delivers nothing after you pay.
Signs of fake shops are a missing legal notice and payment in advance only.
In a love scam, fraudsters pretend to have feelings in order to get money.
In advance-fee fraud, you are supposed to pay money first in order supposedly to receive more later.
With fake support calls you should hang up and not allow remote access.
Sextortion is blackmail using intimate pictures or videos.
Messages about supposed prizes are usually attempts at fraud.

abschnitte.text: A **fake shop** looks like a real online shop, but delivers nothing after you pay. Such shops often tempt people with very low prices for designer clothes, electronics or concert tickets. Warning signs are a missing **legal notice**, payment in advance as the only way to pay, and a strange web address. Before ordering, it is worth searching for reviews of and warnings about the shop.

In a **love scam**, someone pretends to be in love via dating apps or social networks. After weeks of nice messages, the person suddenly needs money, for example for a plane ticket or an operation. In **advance-fee fraud**, you are supposed to pay money first in order supposedly to receive an inheritance or a prize later. But the money promised never comes.

In support fraud, someone phones and pretends to work for a well-known computer company. They claim that your computer has a virus and want to help through remote access. In reality they install malware or access your online banking. The right thing to do is to hang up straight away and not allow any access, because real companies do not call without being asked.

**Sextortion** means blackmail using intimate pictures or videos. The criminals threaten to publish the pictures if you do not pay or send more pictures. Those affected should not pay, should save evidence and should get help from adults and the police immediately. Messages such as “You have won a new mobile phone, click here” are also almost always attempts at fraud.

**Two-factor authentication** asks for a second proof as well as the password when logging in and gives accounts extra protection. You should never pass on passwords, codes or card details, not even to people who claim to work for a bank. If you are asked to pay with a gift card or cryptocurrency, you are almost certainly dealing with fraudsters. In Switzerland you can report attempted fraud to the Federal Office for Cyber Security and report crimes to the police.

begriffe.erklaerung: A fake online shop that delivers nothing.
Information about who is behind a website.
You pay before you have received the goods.
Blackmail using intimate pictures or videos.

gewusst: Advance-fee fraud is older than the internet: in the past, similar begging letters came by post or fax.
Fraudsters often create time pressure, because people think less clearly under stress.

teile.einleitung: Gardeners work outdoors with plants. They lay out gardens, plant flowers and trees, trim hedges and mow the lawn.
wichtigste: Gardeners plant and look after flowers, trees, shrubs and lawns.
They usually work outdoors and in almost all weathers.
Some design and build gardens, others raise plants in a nursery.
The apprenticeship as a gardener EFZ lasts three years.
There is also a two-year training course with a vocational certificate.

abschnitte.text: In **landscape gardening**, gardeners lay out new gardens. They build paths, walls, steps and ponds. They plant trees, shrubs and flowers. Afterwards they **look after** the grounds: they trim **hedges**, mow the **lawn** and remove weeds. Parks and school playgrounds are also cared for in this way.

Other gardeners work in **plant production**. They sow seeds, grow cuttings and look after the young plants in the **greenhouse** or in the field. These include flowers, perennials, vegetable seedlings or young trees in a **tree nursery**. Later the plants are sold.

Gardeners need many tools: a **spade**, rake, shears, watering can and wheelbarrow. For big jobs they use machines, for example lawnmowers, hedge trimmers or small diggers. They also know which plant needs which soil and how much light.

The apprenticeship as a **gardener EFZ** lasts three years. You choose a specialism, for example landscape gardening or plant production. If you would like a shorter training course, you can do the two-year apprenticeship with a vocational certificate (**EBA**). A love of nature and of physical work is important.

gewusst: Gardeners have to know many plant names, often the Latin names too.
After the apprenticeship you can train further, for example up to the master craftsman's examination or at a university of applied sciences.

teile.einleitung: Confectioners are experts in sweet things. In the patisserie they make gateaux, cakes, pastries and chocolates that are often almost too beautiful to eat.
wichtigste: The confectioner makes gateaux, cakes, desserts and chocolates.
People who make chocolates and chocolate are also called chocolatiers (Confiseur or Confiseurin).
In Switzerland the apprenticeship is called baker, pastry chef and confectioner EFZ and lasts three years.
Exact weighing is important, because with dough and cream every gram counts.
Confectioners need skill and a sense for colours and shapes.
The work often starts very early in the morning.

abschnitte.titel: What is made in the patisserie
abschnitte.text: In a **patisserie**, sweet treats are made: gateaux with cream and fruit, cream slices, cakes, biscuits and desserts. For birthdays or weddings, confectioners make **celebration cakes** to order. This also includes **decorating** with glaze, chocolate, marzipan or icing. There is often a small café next to the shop as well.

Making chocolates, truffles and chocolate figures is called **confectionery**. For this, chocolate has to be properly **tempered**: it is warmed and cooled exactly so that it later shines and snaps. Switzerland is famous all over the world for its chocolate. Many confectioners make their chocolates by hand.

In Switzerland you learn the job in the apprenticeship as a **baker, pastry chef and confectioner EFZ** (Bäcker-Konditor-Confiseur EFZ). It lasts three years. You choose a specialism, for example patisserie and confectionery. There is also a two-year basic training course with **EBA**. At vocational school you learn, among other things, how to calculate recipes and about hygiene.

In baking, **precision** is important. Too much flour or too little sugar, and the dough does not turn out well. That is why confectioners weigh everything exactly and pay attention to temperature and time. At the same time they are **creative**: they design gateaux in many shapes and colours. Because the goods should be fresh, the work often starts early in the morning.

gewusst: Zug cherry cake (Zuger Kirschtorte) is a well-known Swiss cake that is soaked with kirsch.
The German word Konditor comes from the Latin “condire”, which means to season or to preserve.

teile.einleitung: An employment contract sets out who works for whom and what pay they get for it. In Switzerland the most important rules on this are in the Code of Obligations.
wichtigste: The individual employment contract is governed by the **Code of Obligations** (OR) from Article 319 onwards.
The two main duties are **doing the work** and **paying the wages**.
An ordinary employment contract needs **no special form**; it is also valid if agreed verbally.
The **apprenticeship contract** must be made in writing.
A fixed-term contract ends on the agreed date without notice.
Unless otherwise agreed in writing, there is a **25 per cent** supplement for overtime.
A **non-competition clause** only applies if it has been agreed in writing.

abschnitte.text: The **individual employment contract** is governed by Articles 319 ff. of the **Code of Obligations** (OR). The OR is actually the fifth part of the Civil Code but is cited as a separate law. According to Art. 319 OR, the employee undertakes to work in the employer's service. In return the employer undertakes to pay **wages**. A typical feature is that you follow the employer's **instructions**.

Under Art. 320 OR an employment contract does not, in principle, need any **particular form**. It can come about verbally or even without words, for example when someone accepts work for pay. Even so, a written contract makes sense, because later you can look up what was agreed. For the **apprenticeship contract**, Art. 344a OR requires written form. It must also be approved by the **cantonal authority**.

A **permanent** contract applies until someone gives notice. Under Art. 334 OR a **fixed-term** contract ends on the agreed date without notice. If you then carry on working without saying anything, the employment is regarded as permanent. With permanent contracts the first month counts as a **probationary period**, during which you can give notice at short notice.

For **overtime**, Art. 321c OR requires the normal wage plus a quarter, a **25 per cent** supplement, unless something else has been agreed in writing. With the employee's agreement, the same amount of time off can be given instead. In the case of **illness** that is not the employee's fault, the employer must continue to pay wages for at least **three weeks** in the first year of service. After that a longer period applies, which is often set according to the Bern, Basel or Zurich **scale**.

With a **non-competition clause** you promise not to go straight to work for a competitor after leaving your job. Under Art. 340 OR it only applies if it was agreed **in writing**. In addition, the person must have had insight into the customer base or business secrets. Except in special circumstances, it may last for no more than **three years**.

gewusst: An employment contract can be valid without a single word ever having been said about it, namely through working for pay without any explicit agreement.
According to the OR, employees are entitled to at least four weeks of holiday a year, and young people up to 20 to five weeks.

teile.einleitung: Florists work with flowers and plants. They tie bouquets, create flower decorations for celebrations and advise their customers in the flower shop.
wichtigste: Florists usually work in a flower shop.
They tie bouquets and make arrangements and wreaths.
They decorate rooms for weddings, celebrations and funerals.
They look after the flowers so that they stay fresh for a long time.
The apprenticeship as a florist EFZ lasts three years.

abschnitte.text: The best-known task is **tying bouquets**. To do this, the florist lays the stems across each other at an angle and turns the bouquet as she goes. This creates a beautiful round shape. At the end she ties the bouquet together and cuts the stems straight.

Florists also create **arrangements**, **wreaths** and table decorations. They decorate churches, halls and tables for weddings, birthdays and company parties. For funerals they make wreaths and grave decorations. They pay attention to colours, shapes and what the customers want.

A florist knows many **flowers and plants** and knows which bloom when. She puts the flowers in fresh water, cuts the stems and removes wilted leaves. Many flowers need to be kept cool, so shops often have a cold room.

In Switzerland the apprenticeship as a **florist EFZ** lasts three years. There is also a two-year training course with a vocational certificate (**EBA**). Important qualities are a love of plants, a sense for colours, skilful hands and enjoying contact with people.

gewusst: Many florists start very early in the morning to buy fresh flowers at the market.
Before Mother's Day and Valentine's Day, flower shops are especially busy.

teile.einleitung: Artificial intelligence, AI for short, is a field of computer science in which computers solve tasks that would otherwise need human intelligence. AI recognises pictures, translates languages, plays games and writes texts. Since chatbots appeared, many people come across AI in everyday life.
wichtigste: AI lets computers solve tasks that otherwise require human intelligence.
In 1950 Alan Turing proposed a test of whether a machine can hold a conversation like a human.
The term artificial intelligence was coined for the Dartmouth Conference in 1956.
In supervised learning, a model learns from examples with known correct answers.
Large language models predict, step by step, the most likely next piece of text.
The transformer architecture of 2017 is the basis of today’s language models.
In 2016 the program AlphaGo beat the Go professional Lee Sedol.

abschnitte.text: **Artificial intelligence** describes computer programs that can learn, recognise, plan or understand language. Today most AI is based on **machine learning**: the program learns from many examples instead of every rule being programmed one by one. In supervised learning it is given examples with the right answers, for example thousands of photos labelled cat or dog. After that it can also classify new photos correctly.

In 1950 the British mathematician **Alan Turing** proposed a test: can a machine hold a conversation in such a way that you cannot tell it apart from a human? The term artificial intelligence was coined for a conference at Dartmouth in the USA in 1956. In 1997 the chess computer Deep Blue beat the world champion Garry Kasparov. In 2016 the program AlphaGo from Google DeepMind beat the Go professional Lee Sedol in a match of five games.

Chatbots such as ChatGPT, which appeared at the end of 2022, are based on **large language models** (LLMs). They have been trained with huge amounts of text and predict, step by step, the most likely next piece of text. The basis is usually the **transformer** architecture, which researchers presented in 2017. Because such models do not really know what is true, they sometimes make up convincing-sounding false statements, which are called hallucinations.

An AI can discriminate even though nobody programmed it to, because it takes on distortions from its **training data**. If an AI used for choosing job applicants learns from old, unfair decisions, it repeats those mistakes. Other risks are fake pictures and voices, data protection problems and the loss of some jobs. That is why you should always check AI results critically.

With the **AI Act**, the EU has passed one of the first comprehensive AI laws, which came into force in 2024. It divides AI systems into levels according to their risk, from minimal risk to forbidden applications. The higher the risk, the stricter the duties that apply. Switzerland is also examining how it wants to regulate AI, taking as one guide a convention of the Council of Europe.

Switzerland is an important location for AI research, for example at ETH Zurich and EPFL in Lausanne. In Ticino, the IDSIA institute in Lugano has been researching learning systems for many years. Many international technology companies have research sites in Zurich. In Switzerland AI is used, for example, in medicine, in weather forecasting and in industry.

begriffe.erklaerung: Computers learn from examples instead of having every rule programmed.
An AI that understands and produces texts by predicting the next word.
A convincingly worded but false statement made by an AI.
The examples from which an AI learns.

gewusst: AlphaGo won four out of five games against Lee Sedol.
The board game Go has so many possible positions that for a long time people believed a computer could never beat a top player.

teile.einleitung: The cockpit is the pilots' workplace. It is right at the front of the aircraft and full of screens, switches and levers used to fly the plane.
wichtigste: The cockpit is where the pilot sits in the aircraft.
It is right at the front of the aircraft.
There are lots of buttons, screens and the controls there.
In big aircraft there are usually two people flying: the captain and the co-pilot.
The pilots talk to air traffic control by radio.
The cockpit door is locked during the flight.

abschnitte.titel: Right at the front of the plane
abschnitte.text: The **cockpit** is right at the front, just behind the nose of the aircraft. The pilots look ahead through big windows. In an airliner there are usually two people sitting side by side. On the left, as a rule, sits the **captain**, and on the right the **co-pilot**, also called the first officer. They share the work and check each other.

Screens show altitude, speed, direction and fuel. With the **control column** or a small **sidestick** the pilots steer the aircraft. With the **thrust levers** they control the power of the engines. An **autopilot** can fly the plane by itself over long distances. Even so, the pilots monitor everything closely.

The pilots talk to **air traffic control** by **radio**. It tells them which altitude and which route are allowed. The language used on the radio is usually English. Before every take-off the pilots go through **checklists** so that nothing is forgotten. This makes flying very safe.

To become an airline pilot you need long and demanding training with theory and many hours in a **flight simulator**. A simulator is a replica cockpit in which you practise flights. Pilots also have to have regular medical checks. Today the **cockpit door** is firmly locked during the flight.

gewusst: The so-called flight recorder, often called the “black box”, is actually orange so that it is easy to find.
A cockpit with lots of screens instead of round dial instruments is called a glass cockpit.

teile.einleitung: The internet is a worldwide network that connects billions of computers, mobile phones and other devices. With it you can send messages, watch videos, learn, play and shop. The World Wide Web, that is, the websites, was invented near Geneva.
wichtigste: The internet connects many computers all over the world.
The abbreviation www stands for World Wide Web.
The World Wide Web was invented at CERN near Geneva.
Being online means being connected to the internet.
At home a router often shares the internet, usually via Wi-Fi.
Not everything on the internet is true.

abschnitte.text: The **internet** is a huge network made of many smaller networks connected to each other. The data travels through cables in the ground, fibre-optic cables on the seabed, by radio and via satellites. Every device on the internet has its own address, the **IP address**, similar to a house address for letters. In 2024 about 5.5 billion people worldwide used the internet.

The forerunner of the internet was called **ARPANET** and from 1969 connected a few universities in the USA. Later people agreed on common rules for how computers exchange data, the so-called TCP/IP. In 1989 the British researcher **Tim Berners-Lee** developed the World Wide Web at CERN near Geneva. With it, pages could be connected with links and looked at easily with a browser.

At home the internet usually comes into the house through a cable or a fibre-optic line. A **router** then shares it with all the devices, often wirelessly through a radio network called **Wi-Fi** (WLAN in German). When you are out and about, your phone connects through the mobile network. If you are connected to the internet, you are online, and if you are not connected, you are offline.

abschnitte.titel: What you can do on the internet
abschnitte.text: On the internet you can write messages and emails, watch videos, listen to music and do research for school. You can also play with friends, check timetables or order books. But some things are not possible directly, for example smelling or tasting something. And the internet does not replace playing outside and meeting friends.

Not everything on the internet is true, because anyone can publish something there. If you are unsure whether something is true, it is best to ask an adult. You do not give personal details such as your address, phone number or passwords to strangers. In Switzerland many websites end in **.ch**, the country ending for Switzerland.

begriffe.erklaerung: A device that shares the internet with all the devices in the house.
A radio network through which devices get onto the internet without cables.
The address of a device on the internet.
A program you use to look at websites.

gewusst: The very first website went online at CERN in 1991 and can still be visited today.
A large part of the world’s internet traffic runs through cables lying on the seabed between the continents.

teile.einleitung: A librarian works in the library. She makes sure that all the books are in their place and that you find the right thing.
wichtigste: A librarian works in the **library**.
In the library you can **borrow** books.
The librarian puts the books in order and helps you look for things.
Every book has a **shelf mark** that shows where it is kept.
Many libraries also have films, audiobooks, games and e-books.
Libraries often organise readings and events for children.

abschnitte.text: In the **library** you can borrow books, comics, audiobooks and films. The **librarian** makes sure that everything is in order. She lends out items, takes them back and puts them back in their place. She helps you search and gives tips on which book might suit you.

So that you can find a book, each one has a fixed place. On the spine there is a small label with the **shelf mark**. It shows which shelf the book is on. In the **catalogue**, usually on a computer, you can search by title, author or topic. The librarian also chooses new books and adds them to the catalogue.

In Switzerland you can do an apprenticeship as an **information and documentation specialist EFZ**. You learn how to sort, find and lend out books and other media. If you go on to study, you can train further at a university of applied sciences. Librarians work in municipal and school libraries, at universities or in big libraries such as the **Swiss National Library** in Bern.

gewusst: The Swiss National Library collects books and other publications that have to do with Switzerland.
In many municipal libraries, borrowing is free for children.

teile.einleitung: Manipulation on the internet means that people are led by hidden tricks to decisions or opinions they might not otherwise have. Behind this are companies that want to sell, or groups that want to stir up political feeling. If you see through the tricks, you can decide more freely.
wichtigste: Dark patterns are design tricks that lead users into decisions against their own interests.
In confirmshaming, the button for saying no has a shaming text.
With a roach motel, it is easy to get in but hard to get out again, for example with a subscription.
Pull to refresh uses irregular rewards like a slot machine.
Astroturfing fakes a spontaneous citizens’ movement.
In the Cambridge Analytica scandal, the data of up to 87 million Facebook users was misused.
A sock puppet is a fake second account that someone uses to support themselves.

abschnitte.text: **Dark patterns** are design tricks on websites and in apps that lead users into decisions against their own interests. The British designer Harry Brignull gave them this name in 2010. One example is **confirmshaming**, where the button for saying no has a shaming text such as “No thanks, I don’t want to save money”. Another is a bright button for “Accept all” next to a barely visible link for refusing.

With a **roach motel** (in German Kakerlakenfalle, a cockroach trap), it is easy to get in but hard to get out again. A subscription, for example, can be taken out with one click, but only cancelled through many hidden steps. Booking websites use artificial scarcity and social pressure, for example with “Only 1 room left, 12 people are looking at this right now”. Such messages are meant to rush you, so that you do not compare calmly.

Features such as **pull to refresh**, pulling down to update, are reminiscent of slot machines. You never know whether something exciting is about to appear, and exactly these unpredictable rewards make you curious. Endless scrolling, videos that start automatically and reward streaks also keep people in apps for longer. So you often spend more time on your phone than you actually wanted.

In **astroturfing**, organised groups fake a spontaneous citizens’ movement. The name comes from AstroTurf, a brand of artificial grass, meaning artificial grass instead of a real grassroots movement. A **sock puppet** is a fake second account with which someone praises or supports themselves. Bought reviews and likes are also among these tricks.

In 2018 it became known that the company **Cambridge Analytica** had used the data of up to 87 million Facebook users. The data originally came from a personality test app that also collected data from the participants’ friends. The company used it for political **microtargeting**, that is, advertising tailored exactly to individual groups. The scandal sparked debates about data protection around the world, and Facebook had to pay a large fine in the USA.

begriffe.erklaerung: A design trick that leads to unwanted decisions.
A faked citizens’ movement.
A fake second account used to support yourself.
Advertising tailored exactly to small groups.

gewusst: With the Digital Services Act, the EU forbids certain dark patterns on online platforms.
The term sock puppet refers to a hand puppet that you move and make speak yourself.

teile.einleitung: The driver's cab is where the train driver works. It is right at the front of the train, so that the driver can see the tracks and the signals well.
wichtigste: The driver's cab is right at the front of the locomotive or the driving trailer.
From there the train driver controls the whole train.
She watches the tracks and signals.
Many trains have a driver's cab at both ends.
Safety systems help to prevent accidents.

abschnitte.text: The **driver's cab** is at the front of the train. Through the large windscreen the train driver can see the **tracks** and the **signals**. Many trains have a driver's cab at both ends. At the final station the driver simply changes ends and drives back in the other direction.

In the driver's cab there is a lever for **accelerating** and **braking**. Screens show the speed, the power and any faults. There are buttons for the doors, lights and windscreen wipers. The train driver talks to the operations centre by radio.

To make sure nothing happens, there are **safety systems**. The **driver vigilance device** regularly checks whether the driver is awake and reacting. If she does not react, the train brakes by itself. A **train protection system** also brakes the train if it would pass a red signal or is going too fast.

Train drivers bring many people and goods safely to their destination every day. They are trained by the railway companies. Many have already completed an apprenticeship in another job before. Concentration, responsibility and punctuality are important, including on shifts early in the morning or late at night.

gewusst: On express trains on new high-speed lines, the signals are shown directly on the screen in the driver's cab.
Switzerland has one of the densest railway networks in the world.

teile.einleitung: The oven is the heart of every bakery. In its heat, soft dough turns into crusty bread.
wichtigste: In the bakery the bread is baked in the big **oven**.
In the hot oven, dough turns into crusty bread.
A bakery oven is much bigger than an oven at home.
Many bakery ovens have several levels, called **decks**.
The heat creates the brown **crust**.
Bakers often start work in the middle of the night.

abschnitte.titel: An oven for lots of loaves
abschnitte.text: In the bakery there is a big **oven**. It is much bigger than an oven in the kitchen at home. Many bakery ovens have several levels one above the other; they are called **deck ovens**. That way lots of loaves, croissants and plaited loaves can be baked at the same time. The heat in the oven is often over 200 degrees.

First the dough is kneaded from flour, water, salt and yeast. Then it is left to rest and **rise**. After that it goes into the hot oven. There the bread becomes soft and airy inside. On the outside a brown, crispy **crust** forms. To make it shine nicely, bakers often put steam into the oven.

So that there is fresh bread in the morning, **bakers** often start in the middle of the night. They knead the dough, shape the loaves and push them into the oven. With a long shovel made of wood or metal they take the finished loaves out. In Switzerland you learn this job in an apprenticeship as a baker-pastry chef-confectioner EFZ.

gewusst: Some bakeries still bake their bread in a **wood-fired oven**, which is heated with wood.
The long shovel used to push loaves into the oven is called a baker's peel.

teile.einleitung: When looking for an apprenticeship, almost all young people also get rejections. A rejection is disappointing, but it is normal, and you can learn a lot from it.
wichtigste: Rejections are part of looking for an apprenticeship.
What matters is staying calm, not giving up and learning from it.
You may politely ask the company for the **reason** for the rejection.
Often another applicant was simply a better fit.
After several rejections it is worth talking to the **careers advice service**.
A **plan B** gives you security in case your dream job does not work out.
You reply to a written rejection briefly and politely with a thank-you.

abschnitte.text: Many young people often apply for the same apprenticeship. But the company can only take one person or a few. That is why most of them get a **rejection**. Often someone else was simply a better fit for the company. So a rejection is **not a judgement of you as a whole person**.

After a rejection you feel disappointed, perhaps sad or angry too. That is understandable. It helps to talk about it with your **parents**, friends or teachers. After that the next step becomes easier. What matters is staying calm and **not giving up**.

You may politely ask the company why it did not work out. Many companies give brief **feedback**. That way you find out what you can do better, for example in your covering letter or at the interview. It is best to reply to a written rejection with a short **thank-you**. This leaves a good impression, and perhaps a place will become free later.

abschnitte.titel: Help from the careers advice service
abschnitte.text: After several rejections it is worth looking at your **application documents** with the careers advice service. The advisers can often see quickly what you can improve. They also give you new ideas. Perhaps a **related job** from the same occupational field would suit you just as well. The advice is usually free for young people.

It does not always work out with your dream job. That is why a **plan B** makes sense. It can be a similar job or an **interim solution**, such as a tenth school year, a work placement or a motivation semester. If you have an alternative ready, you do not lose any time. And sometimes the detour even leads to the goal.

gewusst: Many apprenticeships are only given out in the spring or summer before the apprenticeship starts. So it can still work out even late on.
Some companies get back in touch after a rejection if the person they chose does not take up the place after all.

teile.einleitung: Sleep hygiene does not mean washing in bed, but all the habits that lead to good, restful sleep. These include fixed sleeping times, a quiet room and above all putting your phone away before going to sleep. If you sleep well, you can concentrate better, are happier and learn more easily.
wichtigste: Sleep hygiene means good habits for restful sleep.
Light and exciting content from your phone keep your brain awake.
School-age children need about 9 to 12 hours of sleep a night.
Young people need about 8 to 10 hours of sleep.
Regular bedtimes, even at the weekend, help the body.
The bedroom should be dark, quiet and rather cool.
During sleep, the brain processes what you have learned during the day.

abschnitte.text: **Sleep hygiene** means all the rules and habits that encourage healthy sleep. The word hygiene comes from Greek and has to do with health. Experts recommend about 9 to 12 hours of sleep a night for children between 6 and 12. Young people between 13 and 18 need about 8 to 10 hours.

The screens of phones and tablets give off a lot of **blue light**, which fools the brain into thinking it is still daytime. As a result, the body makes less **melatonin**, a hormone that makes you tired. Even more important are exciting videos, games and chats, which wake the brain up and excite it. That is why it is best to put your phone away an hour before going to sleep, ideally outside the bedroom.

A good bedroom is dark, quiet and rather cool, about 16 to 19 degrees Celsius. The bed should be mainly for sleeping and not for gaming or doing homework. A classic **alarm clock** replaces the phone so that it does not lie next to your pillow. Noise and light from outside can be reduced with curtains or earplugs.

The body has an **internal clock**, which likes regular times. That is why it helps to go to bed and get up at about the same time every day, even at the weekend. An evening routine, for example reading, brushing your teeth and listening to calm music, signals to the brain: now it is time to sleep. Heavy meals, drinks containing caffeine such as cola or iced tea, and wild sport just before sleeping, on the other hand, are disturbing.

During sleep, the brain sorts out the day’s experiences and stores what you have learned in your memory. At the same time, children and young people grow during sleep, because a particularly large amount of growth hormone is released then. If you sleep too little, you are irritable, find it harder to concentrate and get ill more often. In the long term, lack of sleep can also affect weight and mood.

begriffe.erklaerung: A hormone that makes the body tired in the evening.
Light from screens that acts like daylight and keeps you awake.
A natural timer in the body that controls being awake and sleeping.
The same calm activities every time before going to bed.

gewusst: A person spends about a third of their life asleep.
During puberty the internal clock shifts, which is why young people often get tired later in the evening.
Someone who stays up all night reacts as slowly the next day as someone who has drunk alcohol.

teile.einleitung: The captain is responsible for a ship. In Switzerland captains mainly steer passenger boats on the large lakes and ships on the Rhine.
wichtigste: The captain steers the ship and is responsible for it.
Many passenger boats run on the Swiss lakes.
Some of them are historic paddle steamers.
The captain is responsible for the safety of the passengers and the crew.
Cargo ships travel on the Rhine as far as Basel.

abschnitte.text: Many Swiss lakes have **passenger boats**, for example on Lake Lucerne, Lake Geneva, Lake Zurich or Lake Thun. They take commuters and day-trippers from place to place. At the front, in the **wheelhouse**, the captain steers the boat.

The captain is the boss on the ship. He **steers** safely past obstacles and docks gently at the landing stage. He keeps an eye on the **weather** and wind, because a storm can blow up quickly on lakes. He leads the **crew**, who help with docking, check tickets and look after the passengers.

The historic **paddle steamers** are especially well known. They are driven by large paddle wheels at the side. Several of these old ships still sail on Lake Lucerne and Lake Geneva. Many passengers like to look into the engine room, where the steam engine is working.

Via the **Rhine**, cargo ships travel from the North Sea to the **Rhine ports** in Basel. This is how goods such as oil, grain or containers reach Switzerland. Anyone who wants to command a ship needs long training and a special **licence**. On the lakes, many start as deckhands and later become captains.

gewusst: Although Switzerland has no sea, there are ocean-going ships that sail under the Swiss flag.
The port in Basel is Switzerland's only access to the sea by ship.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss Press Council is an independent body that checks whether journalists keep to the ethical rules of their profession. Anyone who thinks a newspaper article, a programme or an online report is unfair or wrong can complain to it. In this way the Press Council helps to make sure that the media in Switzerland report responsibly.
wichtigste: The Swiss Press Council checks whether media professionals keep to ethical rules.
It is based on the “Declaration of the Duties and Rights of Journalists”.
Anyone can submit a complaint to the Press Council free of charge.
The Press Council is set up by the media industry itself, not by the state.
It cannot impose penalties but publishes statements.
The Press Council was founded in 1977.
The most important rules include truth, fairness and the protection of privacy.

abschnitte.text: The **Swiss Press Council** is a complaints body for media such as newspapers, radio, television and online news sites. It was founded in 1977 and is supported by associations of journalists and of publishers. Because the industry checks itself in this way, it is called **self-regulation**. The state deliberately does not get involved, because freedom of the press is protected in the Federal Constitution.

Its work is based on the **“Declaration of the Duties and Rights of Journalists”**, often called the journalists' code. It says, for example, that the media must keep to the truth and check information carefully. They must not leave out facts that are important, and they must correct mistakes. They should also respect people's privacy and not discriminate against anyone.

Anyone can submit a **complaint** to the Press Council, even if they are not affected themselves. It costs nothing and can be done in writing. The Press Council then checks whether the report broke the code. After that it publishes a **statement**, which everyone can read on its website.

The Press Council is not a court and cannot impose fines. Its statements still carry weight, because a reprimand is embarrassing for a media outlet. Many newspapers have committed themselves to publishing the Press Council's reprimands themselves. For radio and television there is also the state Independent Complaints Authority for Radio and Television (UBI).

The media influence what people think about the world and how they vote. In Switzerland's direct democracy careful information is therefore especially important. The Press Council helps the media remain trustworthy. Pupils too can read its statements and learn what makes good **journalism**.

begriffe.erklaerung: A body that checks whether the media report fairly and correctly.
An industry sets its own rules and makes sure they are followed.
A report saying that you think something is wrong or unfair.
The right of the media to report freely without censorship by the state.
The work of gathering, checking and publishing news.

gewusst: Every year the Press Council deals with dozens of complaints about media reports.
Influencers and blogs also come under the code if they work journalistically.
Freedom of the press is set down in Article 17 of the Federal Constitution.

teile.einleitung: An occupational field is a group of jobs with similar activities. If you look at whole occupational fields when choosing a job, you often discover exciting jobs you did not know about.
wichtigste: An **occupational field** groups together jobs with similar activities, materials or places of work.
Healthcare assistant (FaGe) belongs to the **health** occupational field.
Bricklayers belong to the **construction** occupational field.
Farmers, gardeners and forestry workers belong to the **nature** occupational field.
Cooks belong to the **hospitality** industry.
In the same occupational field you can find alternatives to your dream job.

abschnitte.text: There are several hundred apprenticeship trades in Switzerland. To keep track of them, they are divided into **occupational fields**. An occupational field groups together jobs that have similar **activities**, **materials** or **places of work**. This makes it easier to find related jobs. Careers advice and berufsberatung.ch use this classification.

Healthcare assistants, **FaGe** for short, care for and look after people in hospitals, care homes and home care services (Spitex). Their job belongs to the **health** occupational field. Bricklayers build walls and buildings on the building site. Their job belongs to the **construction** occupational field. Both fields are large and offer many different apprenticeships.

Farmers, gardeners and forestry workers work with plants, animals, soil and woodland. They belong to the **nature** occupational field. IT specialists EFZ develop programs or look after computers and networks, which is typical of the **IT** occupational field. Cooks prepare food in restaurants, hotels and canteens. They belong to the **hospitality** industry.

Logistics specialists EFZ make sure that **goods** arrive in the right place. They receive goods, store them and send them on. They work in warehouses, at the post office or for transport companies. This job also belongs to its own occupational field, together with other jobs to do with transport and traffic.

If you fix on just one job, you often overlook **similar jobs**. In the same occupational field there are **alternatives** if your dream job does not work out. For example, if you like working with wood, you can look at carpenter, joiner or wood sculptor. This increases your chances of finding a suitable apprenticeship.

gewusst: Some jobs fit into several occupational fields because they combine different activities.
Many people know only a few jobs, even though there are several hundred apprenticeship trades in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Gymnasium is a secondary school that prepares students for university. It ends with the gymnasial Matura, Matura for short, which opens the way to universities and the ETH.
wichtigste: The Gymnasium ends with the gymnasial Matura.
With the Matura you can in principle go to universities and the ETH without an entrance exam.
The course lasts at least four years.
Every student writes a Matura project.
With the main subject you choose your own focus.
The Confederation and the cantons recognise the Maturas together.

abschnitte.text: In some cantons you start the **long Gymnasium** straight after the 6th year of primary school. You only move to the **short Gymnasium** from secondary school. According to the recognition regulations, the path to the Matura lasts at least **four years**. In some cases a year of secondary school counts towards this.

At the Gymnasium you learn languages, maths, natural sciences, history, art and more. With the **main subject** you choose your own direction. Examples are Latin, biology and chemistry, or economics and law. There is often also a **supplementary subject**.

Every student writes a **Matura project**. This is a larger piece of independent work on a topic you choose yourself. You research, write, build or design something and present the result at the end. This way you learn how scientific work is done.

With the gymnasial Matura you can in principle go to **universities** and the **ETH** without an entrance exam. For medicine there is sometimes an aptitude test. For many courses at a **university of applied sciences** you also need about a year of experience in the world of work, for example an internship.

For a Matura to count throughout Switzerland, it has to be recognised. This is arranged jointly by the **Confederation** and the Swiss Conference of Cantonal Ministers of Education (**EDK**). The Gymnasiums themselves are run by the cantons.

gewusst: Besides the gymnasial Matura, Switzerland also has the vocational Matura and the specialised Matura.
If you do not do the Matura at a Gymnasium, you can also do it later, for example at a Matura school for adults.

teile.einleitung: Career planning means thinking about your own path at work: what interests me, what can I do, where do I want to go? Because the world of work and people change, you do not plan your career just once, but again and again.
wichtigste: John Holland divides career interests into six types, the RIASEC model.
Edgar Schein described career anchors, which are values that people hold on to during their career.
Donald Super showed life roles as the “Life-Career Rainbow”.
With “Planned Happenstance”, John Krumboltz showed that chance events can also be opportunities.
SMART goals help you to express career goals clearly and in a way that can be checked.
Besides the management career path there is the specialist career path for experts.
In Switzerland, viamia offers a free career assessment from the age of 40.

abschnitte.text: The American psychologist **John Holland** sorted career interests into six types: realistic, investigative, artistic, social, enterprising and conventional. From the English initial letters it is called the **RIASEC model**. The “E” stands for “enterprising”: such people like to lead, persuade and sell. Most people fit two or three types, and jobs can be sorted in the same way.

**Edgar Schein** found that people hold on to certain values during their career, for example security, independence or leadership. He called them **career anchors**. **Donald Super** saw a career as a lifelong development. In his **“Life-Career Rainbow”** he shows roles such as learner, worker, citizen or family member, which overlap across the stages of life.

Not everything can be planned. With his approach of **“Planned Happenstance”**, **John Krumboltz** stressed that unplanned events are often important opportunities: a conversation, a holiday job, a new hobby. Curiosity, persistence, flexibility and optimism help you to recognise such chances. So good career planning combines clear goals with openness.

Goals become concrete when they are **SMART**: specific, measurable, attractive, realistic and time-bound. Instead of “I want to improve”, a SMART goal would be something like “I will complete a spreadsheet course by the end of the year”. There are two ways to move up: on the **management career path** you lead a team, on the **specialist career path** you deepen your knowledge as a specialist or expert.

Every canton has a **careers, study and career guidance service**. There, specialists help with choosing a career and with later questions, for example a change of job. With **viamia**, the Confederation and the cantons have created a service that has existed throughout Switzerland since 2022. People aged 40 and over can use it to have their work situation reviewed free of charge and receive recommendations.

gewusst: Many interest tests used in careers advice are based on John Holland's RIASEC model.
Edgar Schein described eight different career anchors.

teile.einleitung: Internet safety means behaving online in a way that keeps you from coming to harm. This includes good passwords, being careful with messages from strangers and having the courage to tell adults about problems. The internet is full of exciting things, but just as in traffic, a few important rules are needed.
wichtigste: If something on the internet seems strange to you, tell an adult.
In Switzerland children and young people with worries can call the number 147.
If you see messages like “You've won, click here”, you do not click.
A computer virus is a harmful program.
You do not open attachments in emails from strangers.
If someone sends you something nasty online, it is not your fault.
If your parents are not there, a teacher, for example, can help.

abschnitte.text: Young children are best surfing where their **parents** are nearby, for example in the living room. There are special search engines and websites for children with checked content. If a website frightens you or something seems strange, close it and tell an adult. Nobody will tell you off for it, because that is exactly the right thing to do.

A **computer virus** is a harmful program that spreads on devices without permission. Such harmful programs, called malware, can steal data, lock files by encrypting them or slow the device down. They often hide in email attachments, in fake free games or behind pop-ups like “You've won, click here”. That is why you do not open attachments from strangers and only download apps from official stores.

Regular **updates** close security gaps in programs and apps. An antivirus program detects many pests before they can do damage. Strong, different passwords and two-factor authentication protect your accounts. Important photos and files should also be saved in a safety copy, a so-called backup.

If someone threatens or insults you online or sends you unpleasant pictures, show it to your parents. It is never your fault if someone sends you something nasty. Take screenshots as evidence, block the person and report them to the platform. Repeatedly picking on someone online is called **cyberbullying**, and some forms of it are criminal offences.

In Switzerland children and young people with worries can reach **Pro Juventute** around the clock on the number **147**, by phone, chat or text message. The advice is free and confidential. If your parents are not there, a teacher, the school social worker or another adult you trust can also help. In the case of crimes you can go to the police.

begriffe.erklaerung: A harmful program that infects devices.
The word for all kinds of harmful programs.
A new version that fixes errors and security gaps.
Repeatedly insulting, threatening or humiliating someone online.
A safety copy of important data.

gewusst: The word “virus” comes from Latin and means poison.
Pro Juventute's 147 advice service can also be reached by chat, text message or email.
Every year in February, Safer Internet Day takes place around the world.

teile.einleitung: Social care workers (Fachfrau or Fachmann Betreuung) support people in everyday life. Many work with small children in a day nursery; others look after older people or people with disabilities.
wichtigste: A social care worker often works with small children in a day nursery.
She plays, does crafts and eats with the children.
Some look after older people or people with disabilities.
The apprenticeship as a social care worker EFZ lasts three years.
The abbreviation for the job is FaBe.

abschnitte.text: In a **day nursery** (Kita), children are looked after while their parents are at work. A social care worker **plays, does crafts and sings** with the children. She goes outside with them and eats with them. With the youngest ones she also changes nappies and puts them down to sleep. She makes sure that every child feels comfortable and safe.

Not all social care workers work with children. Some support **older people** in a care home, while others work with **people with disabilities** in a residential group or a sheltered workshop. They help in everyday life, plan outings and organise free time. In doing so they support people in doing as much as possible for themselves.

The job needs **patience**, empathy and enjoyment of dealing with people. Social care workers work in a **team** and coordinate well with each other. They also talk with parents or relatives. In some places people work shifts, including at weekends.

The apprenticeship as a **social care worker EFZ** lasts three years. You choose a specialism, for example **children, older people** or **people with disabilities**. There is also a general training course. After the apprenticeship you can train further at a **professional education college**, for example in early childhood education.

gewusst: FaBe is the usual abbreviation for Fachfrau or Fachmann Betreuung (social care worker).
The social care apprenticeship is one of the popular apprenticeships in the social field.

teile.einleitung: Wages are the money you get for your work. Apprentices also work in the company and receive apprentice wages for it every month.
wichtigste: In Switzerland apprentices receive apprentice wages every month.
Apprentice wages rise a little with each year of the apprenticeship.
The gross wage is the wage before deductions; the net wage is what is paid out.
Contributions to social insurance such as the AVS are deducted from wages.
Switzerland has no national minimum wage, but some cantons have introduced one.
How high wages are depends on the job, experience and the industry.

abschnitte.text: If you do an apprenticeship, you work in the company and receive **apprentice wages** for it. They are lower than the wages of trained specialists, because you are still learning. The wages rise a little with each **year of the apprenticeship**. How much they are is written in the apprenticeship contract. Many professional associations give **recommendations** on this.

There are two important figures on the payslip. The **gross wage** is the agreed wage. Contributions are deducted from it, for example for the **AVS**, disability insurance and unemployment insurance. What is left is the **net wage**, which is transferred to your account. The deductions are not lost: they protect you, for example in old age or if you become unemployed.

Switzerland has no national **minimum wage**. A popular initiative calling for one was rejected at the ballot box in 2014. However, some **cantons** have introduced their own minimum wage, first the canton of **Neuchâtel**, and later also, for example, Geneva, Jura, Ticino and Basel-City. In many industries, **collective labour agreements** set minimum wages.

Your first wages also bring responsibility. It is worth making a **budget**: how much do I spend on my phone, clothes and free time, and how much do I save? It is often agreed that apprentices contribute part of their wages at home as **board money**. If you learn to handle money early, you avoid debt.

gewusst: The word “salary” comes from the Latin “sal”, which means salt.
From 1 January after their 17th birthday, people in work in Switzerland pay AVS contributions.

teile.einleitung: Bakers make bread, Gipfeli (croissants), Zopf (plaited loaves) and many other baked goods in the bakehouse. Their working day often starts in the middle of the night so that there is fresh bread in the shop in the morning. In Switzerland the apprenticeship is now called baker-pastry chef-confectioner.
wichtigste: Bakers make bread and croissants in the bakehouse.
In Switzerland you learn the job in a three-year apprenticeship with an EFZ.
There is also a two-year basic training course with a Federal VET Certificate (EBA).
Work often begins very early in the morning or even at night.
Important ingredients are flour, water, yeast and salt.
Cleanliness and hygiene are particularly important in the bakehouse.

abschnitte.text: Bakers make **bread**, rolls, croissants and plaited loaves. Many also bake cakes, gateaux, biscuits and pralines. They weigh out the ingredients, knead the dough, let it rise and bake it in the oven. In the end they often sell their goods in their own shop.

The apprenticeship is called baker-pastry chef-confectioner **EFZ** and lasts three years. You choose a specialism, for example bakery and pastry or pastry and confectionery. If you would like something a bit easier, you can do the two-year **EBA** apprenticeship. As well as working at the training company, you attend vocational school and inter-company courses.

So that the bread is fresh in the morning, work often begins at 3 or 4 am. In return the working day is usually over by midday or early afternoon. People often work at weekends too, because that is when customers like to buy a fresh Zopf. The law has special rules on **night work** for young people, which the company must follow.

The most important ingredients for bread are flour, water, salt and **yeast** or sourdough. During fermentation the yeast forms small gas bubbles, which make the dough light and airy. Baking creates the brown, crispy crust. In Switzerland Ruchbrot (dark wheat bread), half-white bread, Zopf and Bürli (crusty rolls) are particularly popular.

Anyone who wants to become a baker should enjoy food and working with their hands. You need good health, because you stand a lot and it is warm in the bakehouse. Precision is important, because recipes must be weighed out exactly. **Hygiene** and teamwork also play a big part.
